spec.n: The Old River in the Fossil Dunes
spec.te: Is the Elephants’ River Inside the Dunes?
spec.desc: A connection between two records on this map. The Baynunah Formation at Mleisa was laid down about seven million years ago by a braided river system with channels three metres deep, and it spreads across Al Dhafra under a thin skin of modern sand. About 100 km to the north-east, the Al Wathba Fossil Dunes are more than 1,700 cemented, cross-bedded dune outcrops dated to about 120,000–150,000 years ago; the accepted story is that their sand blew in from the exposed bed of the Arabian Gulf during dry glacial periods and was then cemented by rising groundwater. The idea: part of the sand in the fossil dunes was not Gulf-floor sediment at all, but Baynunah river sand picked up by the wind as it crossed the eroding Miocene outcrops of Al Dhafra, so that the dunes carry a measurable share of the old river inside them.
spec.sig: If true, the fossil dunes would record not only the glacial sea floor but the slow unmaking of the Miocene river landscape, and sand provenance would become a tool for dating when the Baynunah surface was stripped and when the wind blew from the south-west rather than the north-west.
spec.ev: Mleisa record: Baynunah Formation is river sand and mud with channels 3 m deep, exposed over Al Dhafra, west and south-west of the dunes. Al Wathba Fossil Dunes record: more than 1,700 outcrops in 7 km², dated c. 120,000–150,000 years ago, built from sand that blew in during dry glacial periods and was cemented by groundwater; generations of dunes formed in ice-age cycles between c. 200,000 and 7,000 years ago. Distance: about 100 km between the two records, along the line of the prevailing winds that build the dunes of Abu Dhabi. The abu-dhabi-coastal-sabkha record gives the carbonate, Gulf-derived end member for comparison.
spec.an: Garzanti, Vermeesch, Andò and colleagues (2013) traced the sand of the Arabian deserts to its sources with heavy minerals and detrital zircon ages, showing that the Rub’ al-Khali and the dunes of the Gulf coast are mixtures of sediment carried by ancient rivers from Arabia’s interior and by the Tigris–Euphrates system, and that each source leaves a fingerprint that survives recycling through many generations of dunes (Earth-Science Reviews 120, 1–19).
spec.val: Sample the cemented sand of several fossil-dune generations and the Baynunah river sands at Mleisa; compare grain size, heavy-mineral suites, carbonate versus quartz content and detrital zircon age spectra; use the Gulf-floor carbonate sand of the coastal sabkha as the second end member; estimate the mixing proportion in each dune generation and check whether it changes with age.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: all the dune sand came from the exposed Gulf floor, itself a mix of Tigris–Euphrates and local carbonate sediment, with no Baynunah contribution.

Rival explanation 2: any Baynunah-like fingerprint comes from the Rub’ al-Khali sands to the south, which share older sources with the Miocene river, so the signal cannot be tied to the Baynunah outcrops.
Rival explanation 3: groundwater cementation altered the mineralogy of the dunes so that provenance signals are no longer readable.

spec.se: The sand of a river that elephants crossed seven million years ago lies open to the wind a hundred kilometres upwind of dunes that turned to stone in the ice ages; the dunes may be made partly of that river. Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: رمل نهرٍ عبرته الفيلة قبل سبعة ملايين سنة مكشوفٌ للريح على بعد مئة كيلومتر في اتجاه الريح من كثبان تحجرت في العصور الجليدية؛ وقد تكون الكثبان مصنوعة جزئيًا من ذلك النهر. لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from a coincidence of places and ages on this map. The Mleisa record describes a seven-million-year-old river system exposed across Al Dhafra. The Al Wathba Fossil Dunes record describes sand blown in during the ice ages from the exposed Gulf floor, about 100 km downwind of the river outcrops. Nobody in either record asks whether the river is in the dunes.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من تطابق أماكن وأعمار على هذه الخريطة. يصف سجل مليسا نظامًا نهريًا عمره سبعة ملايين سنة مكشوفًا عبر الظفرة. ويصف سجل كثبان الوثبة المتحجرة رملًا هبّت به الريح في العصور الجليدية من قاع الخليج المكشوف، على بعد نحو 100 كيلومتر في اتجاه الريح من مكاشف النهر. ولا يسأل أي من السجلين عما إذا كان النهر داخل الكثبان.

tag.en: The dunes that turned to rock may be made partly of the river the elephants crossed
tag.ar: قد تكون الكثبان التي تحجرت مصنوعة جزئيًا من النهر الذي عبرته الفيلة

en: Seven million years ago a braided river crossed what is now Al Dhafra. Its sand and mud, the Baynunah Formation, hold elephant footprints at Mleisa and the bones of hippos, giraffes and crocodiles. Today the old river beds lie exposed under a thin skin of modern sand.

About 100 km to the north-east stand the Al Wathba Fossil Dunes: more than 1,700 outcrops of sand that blew in during the ice ages, 120,000–150,000 years ago, and were cemented into stone by groundwater. The usual story says the sand came from the dry floor of the Arabian Gulf.
ar: قبل سبعة ملايين سنة عبر نهر متشعب ما يُعرف اليوم بالظفرة. يحفظ رمله وطينه، تكوين بينونة، آثار أقدام الفيلة في مليسا وعظام أفراس النهر والزرافات والتماسيح. واليوم ترقد مجاري النهر القديمة مكشوفة تحت قشرة رقيقة من الرمل الحديث.

وعلى بعد نحو 100 كيلومتر إلى الشمال الشرقي تقف كثبان الوثبة المتحجرة: أكثر من 1,700 مكشف من رمل هبّت به الريح في العصور الجليدية، قبل 120,000–150,000 سنة، ثم حوّلته المياه الجوفية إلى حجر. والقصة المعتادة تقول إن الرمل جاء من قاع الخليج العربي الجاف.

h2.en: Seen before: the fingerprint of Arabian sand
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: بصمة الرمل العربي

en: In 2013 Eduardo Garzanti and colleagues collected sand from across the Arabian deserts and read each grain like a passport. Heavy minerals and the ages of tiny zircon crystals told them where the sand had started its journey.

They found that the great dune seas are mixtures: sand carried by ancient rivers out of Arabia’s interior, and sand from the Tigris and Euphrates, blown back from the Gulf. Each source left a fingerprint that survived many generations of dunes.
ar: في عام 2013 جمع إدواردو غارزانتي وزملاؤه رملًا من أنحاء الصحارى العربية وقرؤوا كل حبة كأنها جواز سفر. أخبرتهم المعادن الثقيلة وأعمار بلورات الزركون الدقيقة من أين بدأ الرمل رحلته.
ووجدوا أن بحار الكثبان الكبرى خلائط: رمل حملته أنهار قديمة من داخل الجزيرة العربية، ورمل من دجلة والفرات هبّت به الريح عائدًا من الخليج. وترك كل مصدر بصمة بقيت عبر أجيال كثيرة من الكثبان.

en: On this map the old river lies upwind of the fossil dunes. As the wind stripped the Baynunah surface over thousands of years, some of its sand must have gone somewhere. The dunes are a candidate.

If a share of river grains is hiding in the cemented sand, the dunes record two stories at once: the glacial sea floor and the slow erosion of the elephants’ river. If not, the Gulf-floor story stands alone. A few bags of sand and a mass spectrometer could decide.
ar: على هذه الخريطة يقع النهر القديم في اتجاه الريح من الكثبان المتحجرة. وحين جرّدت الريح سطح بينونة على مدى آلاف السنين، لا بد أن بعض رمله ذهب إلى مكان ما. والكثبان مرشحة لذلك.

فإذا كانت حصة من حبيبات النهر مختبئة في الرمل المتحجر، فإن الكثبان تسجل قصتين معًا: قاع البحر الجليدي والتعرية البطيئة لنهر الفيلة. وإن لم تكن، تبقى قصة قاع الخليج وحدها. وبضعة أكياس من الرمل ومطياف كتلة يمكن أن تحسم الأمر.

spec.n: The Lagoon That Fed the Pearling Town
spec.te: Did the Town Live off Its Own Lagoon?
spec.desc: A connection between two records on this map. Al Sinniyah Island, in the Umm Al Quwain lagoon, held the oldest pearling town yet found in the Arabian Gulf, about 12 hectares of houses occupied for about 200 years from the late 6th or early 7th century to the mid-8th century AD, with oyster-shell middens of possibly millions of shells. The same lagoon, Khor Al Beidah, is today a tidal wetland of mudflats, sandflats and mangrove that feeds 350–450 wintering crab plovers and thousands of sand plovers. The idea: the town was placed where it was because the sheltered lagoon itself was a working fishery, and its middens are built mainly from oysters, fish and shellfish gathered inside the lagoon rather than from pearl oysters brought back from offshore banks, so that the modern bird wetland and the ancient town are two readings of one productive system.
spec.sig: If true, the first pearling town of the Gulf would be understood as a lagoon economy as much as an offshore one, and the unprotected Khor Al Beidah would gain a heritage value of thirteen centuries on top of its value for birds.
spec.ev: Al Sinniyah record: town of several thousand people, late 6th/early 7th to mid-8th century AD, houses of local beach rock, pearls, a diver’s weight, and oyster-shell middens of possibly millions of shells; merchants’ courtyard houses beside fishermen’s one- or two-room houses. Khor Al Beidah record: mudflats, sandflats and mangrove supporting 350–450 crab plovers, 1,700–4,000 lesser sand plovers and 850–2,000 greater sand plovers in 2010–2015 counts, with less than 10% of the site protected. Distance: the island sits inside the lagoon; the two records are about 3 km apart.
spec.an: In Denmark, Søren H. Andersen (2000) surveyed the Stone Age shell middens of the Ertebølle culture and showed that their composition tracks the fjords beside them: layers dominated by oysters give way to cockles and mussels as the local waters changed, so that each midden is a record of the fishery at its doorstep (Proceedings of the Prehistoric Society 66, 361–384).
spec.val: Sample the Al Sinniyah middens by layer and identify the species: pearl oysters (Pinctada) from offshore banks versus edible oysters, clams and fish bones from lagoon habitats; measure shell sizes and growth lines to see where and in which season they were gathered; compare with the present species of Khor Al Beidah; core the lagoon sediments to test whether the mudflats and mangroves already existed in the 7th century.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the middens are almost entirely pearl oyster from the offshore banks, and the lagoon served only as a sheltered harbour.
Rival explanation 2: the lagoon of the 7th century was deeper and more open than today’s mudflats, so the modern wetland is not the one the town knew.
Rival explanation 3: the town’s food came mainly by trade, as the 12% of imported Indian pottery suggests, and local gathering was marginal.
refs: Power, T., Degli Esposti, M., Hoyland, R. et al. (2024). Excavations at a late antique to early Islamic pearling town and monastery on Sīnīya Island, Umm al-Quwain. Proceedings of the Seminar for Arabian Studies 53: 211–229.
Dennehy, J. (2023). Oldest pearling town in the Arabian Gulf discovered in Umm Al Quwain. The National, 20 March 2023.
BirdLife International (2017). Important Bird Area factsheet: Khor Al Beidah, United Arab Emirates.
Andersen, S.H. (2000). "Køkkenmøddinger" (shell middens) in Denmark: a survey. Proceedings of the Prehistoric Society 66, 361–384.
spec.se: The lagoon that feeds thousands of plovers today may be the same larder that fed a town of several thousand people and millions of shells thirteen centuries ago. Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: الخور الذي يطعم آلاف الزقزاقات اليوم قد يكون المخزن نفسه الذي أطعم بلدة من عدة آلاف من الناس وملايين الأصداف قبل ثلاثة عشر قرنًا. لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from a coincidence of places on this map. The Al Sinniyah record describes middens of possibly millions of shells on an island inside the Umm Al Quwain lagoon. The Khor Al Beidah record describes the same lagoon as a wetland rich enough to feed thousands of shorebirds, with less than 10% of it protected. One lagoon, two records, no link between them yet.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من تطابق أماكن على هذه الخريطة. يصف سجل السينية أكوامًا من الأصداف ربما بلغت الملايين على جزيرة داخل خور أم القيوين. ويصف سجل خور البيضاء الخور نفسه أرضًا رطبة غنية بما يكفي لإطعام آلاف الطيور الشاطئية، مع حماية أقل من 10% منه. خور واحد، وسجلان، ولا رابط بينهما بعد.

en: On Al Sinniyah Island, inside the lagoon of Umm Al Quwain, archaeologists found a town of hundreds of houses and several thousand people, lived in for about 200 years from the late 6th or early 7th century. Behind the houses were middens of oyster shells, possibly millions of them.

The lagoon around the island, Khor Al Beidah, is today a wetland of mudflats and mangrove. Counts in 2010–2015 found 350–450 crab plovers and thousands of sand plovers wintering here, feeding on the worms, crabs and shellfish of the mud. Less than 10% of it is protected.
ar: على جزيرة السينية، داخل خور أم القيوين، وجد الآثاريون بلدة من مئات البيوت وعدة آلاف من الناس، سُكنت نحو 200 عام من أواخر القرن السادس أو أوائل السابع. وخلف البيوت أكوام من أصداف المحار، ربما بالملايين.

والخور المحيط بالجزيرة، خور البيضاء، هو اليوم أرض رطبة من الطين والقرم. وجدت تعدادات 2010–2015 هنا 350–450 زقزاقًا من زقزاقات السرطان وآلافًا من زقزاقات الرمل تقضي الشتاء، تتغذى على ديدان الطين وسرطاناته وأصدافه. ومحميّ منه أقل من 10%.

h2.en: Seen before: the shell middens of Denmark
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: أكوام الأصداف في الدنمارك

en: Along the fjords of Denmark, Stone Age people piled up shell middens that archaeologists have studied for more than a century. In 2000 Søren Andersen surveyed them all and showed that each heap is a diary of the water beside it.

Where the fjords were salty, the layers are full of oysters. As the water freshened, oysters gave way to cockles and mussels. The middens did not record distant fishing grounds; they recorded the larder at the doorstep.
ar: على طول مضايق الدنمارك كوّم أناس العصر الحجري أكوامًا من الأصداف درسها الآثاريون أكثر من قرن. وفي عام 2000 مسحها سورين أندرسن كلها وبيّن أن كل كومة يوميات للماء الذي بجانبها.
فحيث كانت المضايق مالحة امتلأت الطبقات بالمحار. وحين عذب الماء حلّ محل المحار القواقع وبلح البحر. لم تسجل الأكوام مصايد بعيدة، بل سجلت المخزن على عتبة الباب.

en: On this map the two records sit 3 km apart in the same water. The town’s pearls came from offshore banks, but a town of thousands needs dinner every day, and the mud of the lagoon is a kitchen that never closes.

Were the middens mostly pearl oysters, or mostly lagoon food? Were the mudflats even there in the 7th century? A few buckets of shells, sorted by species, and a core through the lagoon mud could join the birds and the town into one story, or keep them apart.
ar: على هذه الخريطة يقع السجلان على بعد 3 كيلومترات في الماء نفسه. جاء لؤلؤ البلدة من مغاصات بعيدة، لكن بلدة من آلاف الناس تحتاج إلى عشاء كل يوم، وطين الخور مطبخ لا يغلق أبدًا.

هل كانت الأكوام محار لؤلؤ في معظمها أم طعام الخور؟ وهل كان الطين موجودًا أصلًا في القرن السابع؟ بضعة دلاء من الأصداف مصنّفة حسب النوع، وعينة لبية عبر طين الخور، يمكن أن تجمع الطيور والبلدة في قصة واحدة، أو تبقيهما متباعدتين.

spec.n: The Ridge People Kept Coming Back To
spec.na: الحافة التي ظلّ الناس يعودون إليها
spec.te: Did the Limestone Ridges Make Faya a Refuge?
spec.ta: هل جعلت الحواف الجيرية الفاية ملاذًا؟
spec.desc: A connection between four records on this map. Around Jebel Faya in central Sharjah, 18 distinct layers of human activity span more than 210,000 years, with handaxes, blades and points about 125,000 years old; the site is seen as a key place for how early humans crossed and survived Arabia through its wet and dry phases. A few kilometres to the north, Fossil Rock and the ridge of Jebel Maleihah are marine limestone laid down from the Late Cretaceous to the Paleocene on top of the Samail Ophiolite. About 12 km to the south, the limestone ridge of Jebel Buhais, with fossils at least 93 million years old, runs almost continuously from Madam to Mleiha and carries a Neolithic cemetery of about 5000–4000 BC whose burials are read as those of herders who came inland for the winter. The idea: the line of fractured limestone ridges resting on ophiolite works as a natural store of water and shelter, so that rain soaking into the limestone seeps out again along the ridge feet; this, and not only the wet phases, is why people returned to Faya again and again and why herders chose Buhais for their winters.
spec.sig: If true, the long record of Faya would be explained by a geological structure that it shares with Fossil Rock and Jebel Buhais, and the whole ridge line from Madam to Mleiha would be a single place of refuge to survey for further sites of every age.
spec.ev: Faya Palaeolandscape record: 18 layers of human activity spanning more than 210,000 years; stone tools about 125,000 years old (2011); a landscape of dunes, rocky outcrops and fossil remnants; World Heritage 2025. Fossil Rock record: a few kilometres north of Jebel Faya; marine limestone, Late Cretaceous to early–mid Paleocene, on top of the Samail Ophiolite; Jebel Faya 412 m. Buhais Geology Park record: limestone ridge with fossils at least 93 million years old, running almost continuously from Madam to Mleiha. Jebel Buhais record: outcrop rising to about 340 m on the same ridge; cemetery BHS 18 dated about 5000–4000 BC with about 600 individuals, read as herders who came inland for the winter. Distances: Faya to Fossil Rock about 3 km; Faya to Jebel Buhais about 12 km.
spec.an: Breeze, Groucutt, Drake and colleagues (2016) mapped ancient rivers, lakes and wetlands across the Middle East from satellite data and dated deposits, and argued that in wet phases these formed corridors of fresh water along which early humans could move and survive; where water was found, the archaeology followed (Quaternary Science Reviews 144, 155–185).
spec.val: Survey the feet of the Faya, Maleihah and Buhais ridges for old spring and seep deposits, such as spring carbonates, and date them; compare their ages with the 18 occupation layers at Faya and the Neolithic cemetery at Buhais; map the contact between the limestone and the ophiolite beneath and test whether shallow groundwater collects along it today; check whether occupation at Faya continued into dry phases when the open desert around it was empty.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: people came only in wet phases, when the whole landscape held water, and the ridges played no special part.
Rival explanation 2: the ridges mattered for shelter, stone or as landmarks on a route, not for water.
Rival explanation 3: the long sequence at Faya is a matter of preservation: sediment trapped at the foot of the mountain kept the layers, while camps in the open desert were blown away.
refs: Current World Archaeology (2025). Faya Palaeolandscape becomes only site in the Arab world to be awarded UNESCO World Heritage status in 2025.
UNESCO World Heritage Centre. Faya Palaeolandscape, inscribed 2025.
NASA Earth Observatory (2025). Digging Back in Time in the UAE (Landsat 8 image of 23 October 2025).
Sharjah Environment and Protected Areas Authority. Buhais Geology Park.
Uerpmann, H.-P., Uerpmann, M. & Jasim, S. A. (2006). Funeral Monuments and Human Remains from Jebel al-Buhais. Department of Culture and Information, Sharjah.

Breeze, P.S., Groucutt, H.S., Drake, N.A., White, T.S., Jennings, R.P. & Petraglia, M.D. (2016). Palaeohydrological corridors for hominin dispersals in the Middle East ∼250–70,000 years ago. Quaternary Science Reviews 144, 155–185.
spec.se: People kept returning to Faya for 210,000 years, and herders wintered on the next ridge 6,000 years ago. Both sit on limestone ridges lying over ancient ocean crust. Did the rock hold the water that held the people? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: ظلّ الناس يعودون إلى الفاية 210,000 عام، وقضى الرعاة الشتاء على الحافة المجاورة قبل 6,000 عام. وكلاهما على حواف جيرية فوق قشرة محيطية قديمة. فهل حبس الصخر الماء الذي أبقى الناس؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from a coincidence of places on this map. The Faya record describes 18 layers of people over 210,000 years. The Fossil Rock and Buhais Geology Park records describe marine limestone ridges over the Samail Ophiolite, running from Madam to Mleiha. The Jebel Buhais record puts Neolithic herders’ winter burials on the same ridge line.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من تطابق أماكن على هذه الخريطة. يصف سجل الفاية 18 طبقة من البشر على مدى 210,000 عام. ويصف سجلا جبل الفوسيل وحديقة البحيص الجيولوجية حوافَّ من الحجر الجيري البحري فوق أفيوليت سمائل، تمتد من مدام إلى مليحة. ويضع سجل جبل البحيص مدافن الرعاة الشتوية من العصر الحجري الحديث على خط الحواف نفسه.

title.en: The Rock That Held the Water

tag.en: A line of limestone ridges in Sharjah may explain 210,000 years of people coming back
tag.ar: ربما يفسّر خط من الحواف الجيرية في الشارقة عودة الناس 210,000 عام

en: Around Jebel Faya in Sharjah, archaeologists have found 18 layers of human life, one above another, going back more than 210,000 years. Some layers hold handaxes, blades and points about 125,000 years old. People came, left, and came back, through wet times and dry times.

Just to the north, Fossil Rock is full of shells and sea urchins from an old sea floor: limestone lying on top of the Samail Ophiolite, a slice of ancient ocean crust. To the south the limestone ridge of Jebel Buhais carries the graves of herders who came inland for the winter, about 5000–4000 BC.
ar: حول جبل الفاية في الشارقة وجد الآثاريون 18 طبقة من حياة البشر، واحدة فوق الأخرى، تعود إلى أكثر من 210,000 عام. وفي بعض الطبقات فؤوس يدوية ونصال ورؤوس عمرها نحو 125,000 عام. جاء الناس ورحلوا ثم عادوا، في الأزمنة الرطبة والجافة.

وإلى الشمال مباشرة يمتلئ جبل الفوسيل بأصداف وقنافذ بحر من قاع بحر قديم: حجر جيري يرقد فوق أفيوليت سمائل، وهو شريحة من قشرة محيطية قديمة. وإلى الجنوب تحمل حافة جبل البحيص الجيرية قبور رعاة جاؤوا إلى الداخل في الشتاء، نحو 5000–4000 ق.م.

en: In 2016 Paul Breeze and colleagues used satellite images and dated lake and river deposits to map where fresh water lay across the Middle East during the wet phases of the last few hundred thousand years.

They found that rivers, lakes and wetlands formed corridors across land that is desert today, and argued that early humans moved and survived along them. Where the water was, the archaeology followed.
ar: في عام 2016 استخدم بول بريز وزملاؤه صور الأقمار الصناعية ورواسب البحيرات والأنهار المؤرخة لرسم خريطة لمواضع الماء العذب في الشرق الأوسط خلال المراحل الرطبة في مئات آلاف السنين الأخيرة.
ووجدوا أن الأنهار والبحيرات والأراضي الرطبة شكّلت ممرات عبر أرض هي اليوم صحراء، ورأوا أن البشر الأوائل تنقّلوا وعاشوا على امتدادها. وحيث كان الماء، تبعته الآثار.

en: On this map Faya, Fossil Rock and Jebel Buhais sit on one line of limestone ridges over ocean crust. Rain that sinks into cracked limestone may be held above the rock beneath and seep out at the ridge feet. If so, the ridges were a small water corridor of their own, even in dry times.

Or perhaps not. People may have come only when the whole land was green, or for shelter and stone. Old spring deposits at the foot of the ridges, dated and compared with the layers at Faya, could tell which story is true.
ar: على هذه الخريطة تقع الفاية وجبل الفوسيل وجبل البحيص على خط واحد من الحواف الجيرية فوق قشرة المحيط. والمطر الذي يتسرّب في الحجر الجيري المتشقق قد يُحبس فوق الصخر الذي تحته ثم ينزّ عند أقدام الحواف. وإن كان ذلك صحيحًا، فالحواف ممر ماء صغير خاص بها، حتى في الأزمنة الجافة.
وربما لا. فقد يكون الناس جاؤوا فقط حين اخضرّت الأرض كلها، أو طلبًا للمأوى والحجر. ورواسب الينابيع القديمة عند أقدام الحواف، إذا أُرّخت وقورنت بطبقات الفاية، يمكن أن تبيّن أي القصتين هي الصحيحة.

spec.te: Does a Mangrove Need to Grow Old Before Its Rarest Birds Arrive?
spec.ta: هل يجب أن يشيخ القرم قبل أن تأتيه أندر طيوره؟
spec.desc: A connection between three records on this map. On the Gulf of Oman coast, Khor Kalba holds the tallest and most extensive mature mangrove woodland of grey mangrove, Avicennia marina, in the region; it is described as a relict forest, and it is almost the only breeding place of the Kalba white-collared kingfisher, an endemic subspecies, and one of only two regional breeding sites of Sykes’s warbler. On the Arabian Gulf coast, the Mangrove National Park of Abu Dhabi covers about 10 km² of the same species, 2–4 m tall, in forests restored since the 1970s; Al Zorah in Ajman protects 195 hectares with some of the few mangroves left in the northern Emirates, and 6,600 saplings were planted there in 2023. The idea: what makes Kalba special for its rare birds is not the size of its forest but its age and height, so that the younger forests on the Arabian Gulf coast will not hold these birds until they grow a structure like Kalba’s.
spec.sig: If true, mangrove planting in the Emirates should be measured not only in trees and square kilometres but in the decades needed to grow old forest, and Kalba’s mature woodland would be irreplaceable within a human lifetime.
spec.ev: Khor Kalba record: 1,494 ha, Ramsar 10 March 2013; tallest and most extensive mature mangrove woodland in the biogeographic region; Kalba white-collared kingfisher (Todiramphus chloris kalbaensis) breeds almost exclusively here; Sykes’s warbler has one of its two regional breeding sites here; hawksbill and green turtles feed in the creeks. Mangrove National Park record: about 10 km² of Avicennia marina, 2–4 m tall; restoration begun in the 1970s; flamingos, western reef herons, crabs, turtles, dugongs and dolphins recorded. Al Zorah record: 195 ha, protected since 2004, Ramsar 2018; among the few remaining mangroves of the northern Emirates; 108 animal species and more than 50 bird species; 6,600 saplings planted over 0.9 ha on 24 November 2023. Distances: Kalba to Al Zorah about 100 km, to Abu Dhabi about 200 km, across the Hajar Mountains.
spec.an: In Oregon, Forsman, Meslow and Wight (1984) studied the northern spotted owl and found it closely tied to old-growth conifer forest; young managed stands did not replace it, so the owl’s future depended on the age of the forest, not just its area (Wildlife Monographs 87).
spec.val: Lay out matching survey plots in Khor Kalba, Al Zorah and the Mangrove National Park; measure tree height, trunk thickness and stand age in each; map the nests and territories of the Kalba kingfisher and Sykes’s warbler at Kalba against the same measures; survey the Arabian Gulf forests for both species; compare water temperature, salinity and tide at the three sites to separate the effect of forest age from the effect of the sea.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the birds are held at Kalba by the Hajar Mountains and the distance between the two coasts, not by the trees; they simply cannot reach the western forests.
Rival explanation 2: the hotter, saltier water of the Arabian Gulf keeps its mangroves short whatever their age, so the western forests can never grow like Kalba.
Rival explanation 3: the birds depend on Kalba’s other habitats, such as its salt marsh, tidal channels and Acacia woodland, rather than on the age of the mangroves.
refs: Ramsar Sites Information Service. Mangrove and Al Hafeya Protected Area in Khor Kalba (site 2125), designated 2013.

spec.se: The Emirates are planting millions of mangroves, and Abu Dhabi alone has about 10 km² of them. Yet a kingfisher found nowhere else breeds almost only in the old, tall trees of Khor Kalba. Is age the thing that cannot be planted? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: تزرع الإمارات ملايين أشجار القرم، وفي أبوظبي وحدها نحو 10 كيلومترات مربعة منها. ومع ذلك فإن رفرافًا لا يوجد في أي مكان آخر يتكاثر تقريبًا في أشجار خور كلباء العتيقة الطويلة وحدها. فهل العمر هو ما لا يمكن زرعه؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from a contrast between records on this map. The Khor Kalba record describes the tallest, most mature mangroves of the region and two rare breeding birds. The Mangrove National Park and Al Zorah records describe younger, restored or newly planted forests of the same tree on the Arabian Gulf coast, restored and planted since the 1970s, without those birds.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من تباين بين سجلات على هذه الخريطة. يصف سجل خور كلباء أطول أشجار القرم في المنطقة وأكثرها نضجًا وطائرين نادرين يتكاثران فيها. ويصف سجلا منتزه القرم الوطني والزوراء غابات أحدث عمرًا من الشجرة نفسها على ساحل الخليج العربي، أُعيد تأهيلها وزُرعت منذ السبعينيات، دون ذينك الطائرين.

test.ar: قياس طول الأشجار وسماكة جذوعها وأعمارها في مربعات مسح في المواقع الثلاثة، ورسم خريطة للطيور المتكاثرة في كلباء مقابل هذه القياسات، ومسح الغابات الغربية بحثًا عن الطائرين، ومقارنة ظروف البحر في كل موقع.

wrong.en: If the Kalba birds breed as readily in young or short stands as in old ones, or if western forests that already match Kalba’s structure still lack them, age is not the key and the idea fails.

title.en: The Forest That Cannot Be Planted

tag.en: Millions of new mangroves, and one kingfisher that may be waiting for them to grow old
tag.ar: ملايين من أشجار القرم الجديدة، ورفراف واحد ربما ينتظرها حتى تشيخ

en: At Khor Kalba, on the Gulf of Oman coast of Sharjah, grows the tallest and most extensive mature mangrove woodland in the region. It is a relict forest, a survivor. In it breeds a kingfisher with a white collar, a subspecies found almost nowhere else on Earth, and Sykes’s warbler, at one of only two breeding places in the region.

On the Arabian Gulf coast the mangroves are younger. In Abu Dhabi, about 10 km² of grey mangrove, 2–4 m tall, has been restored since the 1970s. In Ajman, Al Zorah protects some of the last mangroves of the northern Emirates, and 6,600 young trees were planted there in 2023.
ar: في خور كلباء، على ساحل خليج عُمان في الشارقة، تنمو أطول غابة قرم ناضجة وأوسعها في المنطقة. إنها غابة متبقية، ناجية من زمن مضى. ويتكاثر فيها رفراف أبيض الطوق، سلالة لا تكاد توجد في أي مكان آخر على الأرض، وكذلك دخلة سايكس في أحد موقعين فقط لتكاثرها في المنطقة.

أما على ساحل الخليج العربي فأشجار القرم أصغر سنًّا. ففي أبوظبي أُعيد تأهيل نحو 10 كيلومترات مربعة من القرم الرمادي بطول 2–4 أمتار منذ السبعينيات. وفي عجمان تحمي الزوراء بعضًا من آخر أشجار القرم في الإمارات الشمالية، وزُرعت فيها 6,600 شجرة فتية عام 2023.

h2.en: Seen before: the owl of the old forest
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: بومة الغابة العتيقة

en: In the forests of Oregon, in the United States, Eric Forsman and colleagues followed the northern spotted owl for years. In 1984 they showed that it lived in old-growth forest, among huge, ancient trees.
Young forests, even large ones, did not take its place. The owl taught foresters a hard lesson: you can plant a forest in a year, but you cannot plant an old forest. Only time makes one.
ar: في غابات أوريغون بالولايات المتحدة تتبّع إريك فورسمان وزملاؤه البومة المرقطة الشمالية سنوات. وفي عام 1984 بيّنوا أنها تعيش في الغابات العتيقة، بين أشجار ضخمة قديمة.
ولم تحلّ الغابات الفتية محلها، حتى الكبيرة منها. وعلّمت البومة مهندسي الغابات درسًا صعبًا: يمكنك أن تزرع غابة في عام، لكنك لا تستطيع أن تزرع غابة عتيقة. الزمن وحده يصنعها.

en: On this map the old forest of Kalba and the young forests of Abu Dhabi and Ajman are the same tree on two coasts. Perhaps the kingfisher is waiting for the young forests to grow tall and old, and one day it will find them.

Or perhaps the mountains between the coasts keep it away, or the hotter, saltier water of the Arabian Gulf keeps the trees short for ever. Measuring trees and mapping nests in all three forests could tell us which.
ar: على هذه الخريطة غابة كلباء العتيقة وغابات أبوظبي وعجمان الفتية هي الشجرة نفسها على ساحلين. ربما ينتظر الرفراف أن تطول الغابات الفتية وتشيخ، وسيجدها يومًا ما.
وربما تمنعه الجبال التي بين الساحلين، أو تُبقي مياه الخليج العربي الأشد حرارة وملوحة الأشجار قصيرة إلى الأبد. وقياس الأشجار ورسم خرائط الأعشاش في الغابات الثلاث يمكن أن يخبرنا أيّها الصحيح.

spec.n: Stones from the Mountain for the Dead
spec.te: Did the Tomb Builders Choose Their Stone from Jebel Jais?
spec.ta: هل اختار بناة المدافن حجارتهم من جبل جيس؟
spec.desc: A connection between three records on this map. At Shimal, about 8 km north-east of Ras Al Khaimah town, a cemetery of about 250 tombs includes the Umm an-Nar tomb Sh 222, 11.3 m across with about 300 burials (c. 2200–2000 BC), and Wadi Suq tombs such as Sh 99, 16 m long, and Sh 102, of the 15th–13th centuries BC. At Dhayah, about 8 km further on, twelve Wadi Suq tombs of c. 2000–1300 BC lie at the base of a hill between the date gardens and the Jebel Jais mountains. Jebel Jais itself, the highest peak of the Emirates, exposes marine and terrestrial sedimentary rocks with fossils, and the Hajar range holds ophiolites. The idea: the builders of these monumental tombs did not simply pick up the nearest boulders, but chose particular kinds of rock from the mountain front, and the choice changed between the Umm an-Nar and the Wadi Suq periods.
spec.sig: If true, the tombs of Shimal and Dhayah would record not only how people buried their dead but how they knew and used the rocks of the Hajar Mountains, and a change in stone could mark a change in who built them and why.
spec.ev: Shimal record: about 250 tombs of several types, settled for at least 4,500 years; Umm an-Nar tomb Sh 222, 11.3 m across, about 300 burials, c. 2200–2000 BC; Wadi Suq tombs Sh 99 (16 m long, at least 66 individuals) and Sh 102 (about 140 individuals, 15th–13th centuries BC); soft-stone vessels among the finds. Dhayah Fort record: hill about 70 m high between the date gardens and the Jebel Jais mountains; Late Bronze Age settlement c. 1600–1300 BC; twelve Wadi Suq tombs of c. 2000–1300 BC at its base, four excavated. Jebel Jais record: summit 1,934 m; marine and terrestrial sedimentary rocks with fossils; Hajar range with ophiolites; formations more than 70 million years old. Distances: Shimal to Dhayah about 8 km; both within about 9–17 km of the summit of Jebel Jais.
spec.an: Parker Pearson and colleagues (2015) showed that some of the bluestones of Stonehenge came from Craig Rhos-y-felin in the Preseli Hills of west Wales, by matching the rock of the monument to particular outcrops and finding traces of Neolithic quarrying there; the builders had chosen a specific rock from a specific place (Antiquity 89, 1331–1352).
spec.val: Record the rock type of every visible stone in a sample of Umm an-Nar and Wadi Suq tombs at Shimal and Dhayah; count the rock types in the wadi gravels and slopes next to each tomb; compare the two sets; trace any rock types that are over-represented in the tombs to outcrops on the Jais mountain front through thin sections and chemistry; compare the choices of the two periods.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the builders used whatever boulders lay nearest, and the tombs simply mirror the local gravels.
Rival explanation 2: stones were taken from older tombs and reused, so any pattern of choice has been blurred.
Rival explanation 3: stones were chosen for their size and shape, not their rock type, and any match to a source is a by-product.
refs: Emirates Natural History Group. Shimal Archaeological Site (enhg.org).
Hellyer, P. and Potts, D. (2012). Fifty Years of Emirates Archaeology. Abu Dhabi, pp. 216–221.
Ras Al Khaimah Department of Antiquities and Museums. Dhayah Fort (rakheritage.rak.ae).
Visit Ras Al Khaimah. The ancient story beneath the slopes: Jebel Jais history and geology explained.
Parker Pearson, M., Bevins, R., Ixer, R. et al. (2015). Craig Rhos-y-felin: a Welsh bluestone megalith quarry for Stonehenge. Antiquity 89(348), 1331–1352.
spec.se: The great tombs of Shimal and Dhayah stand at the foot of Jebel Jais, a mountain of sea-floor rock in a range that holds ancient ocean crust. Did their builders pick up any stone, or choose stones from the mountain on purpose? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: تقف مدافن شمل وضاية الكبيرة عند سفح جبل جيس، جبلٍ من صخور قاع البحر في سلسلة تضم قشرة محيطية قديمة. فهل التقط بناتها أي حجر، أم اختاروا حجارة الجبل عن قصد؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from a coincidence of places on this map. The Shimal and Dhayah records describe monumental Umm an-Nar and Wadi Suq tombs a few kilometres apart at the mountain foot. The Jebel Jais record describes the many kinds of rock that the same mountains offer. Nobody in these records asks which rocks the builders used.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من تطابق أماكن على هذه الخريطة. يصف سجلا شمل وضاية مدافن ضخمة من فترتي أم النار ووادي سوق تفصلها كيلومترات قليلة عند سفح الجبل. ويصف سجل جبل جيس أنواع الصخر الكثيرة التي تقدّمها الجبال نفسها. ولا يسأل أي من هذه السجلات أيّ الصخور استعمل البناؤون.

title.en: The Builders Who Read the Rocks

tag.en: The great tombs of Ras Al Khaimah may be built from stones chosen on the mountain
tag.ar: ربما بُنيت مدافن رأس الخيمة الكبيرة من حجارة اختيرت على الجبل

en: At Shimal, near Ras Al Khaimah, about 250 tombs lie at the foot of the mountains. One of them, Sh 222, is 11.3 metres across and held about 300 people buried around 2200–2000 BC. Later tombs of the Wadi Suq period include Sh 99, which is 16 metres long.

A few kilometres away, twelve more Wadi Suq tombs lie at the base of the hill of Dhayah. Behind them rises Jebel Jais, the highest mountain in the Emirates, made of sedimentary rocks with fossils, and part of a range that also holds slices of ancient ocean crust.
ar: في شمل قرب رأس الخيمة يرقد نحو 250 مدفنًا عند سفح الجبال. قطر أحدها، Sh 222، يبلغ 11.3 مترًا، وضمّ نحو 300 شخص دُفنوا نحو 2200–2000 ق.م. ومن المدافن اللاحقة من فترة وادي سوق المدفن Sh 99 الذي يبلغ طوله 16 مترًا.

وعلى بعد كيلومترات قليلة يرقد اثنا عشر مدفنًا آخر من فترة وادي سوق عند قاعدة تل ضاية. ومن خلفها يرتفع جبل جيس، أعلى جبل في الإمارات، المكوّن من صخور رسوبية فيها أحافير، وهو جزء من سلسلة تضم أيضًا شرائح من قشرة محيطية قديمة.

h2.en: Seen before: the bluestones of Stonehenge
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: الحجارة الزرقاء في ستونهنج

en: Some of the stones of Stonehenge in England are not local. In 2015 Mike Parker Pearson and colleagues matched them to a rocky outcrop called Craig Rhos-y-felin, in the Preseli Hills of west Wales, and found there the traces of ancient quarrying.

The builders had not taken just any stone. They had chosen one particular rock from one particular place, and carried it a very long way. The stones of a monument became a map of what its builders knew.
ar: بعض حجارة ستونهنج في إنجلترا ليست محلية. وفي عام 2015 طابقها مايك باركر بيرسون وزملاؤه مع مكشف صخري اسمه كريغ روس-إي-فيلين في تلال بريسيلي غربي ويلز، ووجدوا هناك آثار مقلع قديم.
لم يأخذ البناؤون أي حجر كيفما اتفق، بل اختاروا صخرًا بعينه من مكان بعينه، وحملوه مسافة بعيدة جدًا. وصارت حجارة المعلم خريطة لما كان بناته يعرفونه.

en: On this map the tombs of Shimal and Dhayah sit within a short walk of a mountain that offers many kinds of rock. If the builders chose some rocks over others, and if the Wadi Suq builders chose differently from those of Umm an-Nar, the walls of the tombs still hold that knowledge.

Or perhaps they used whatever lay nearest, or took stones from older tombs. Counting the rocks in the tomb walls and in the gravel beside them is simple fieldwork, and it could tell these stories apart.
ar: على هذه الخريطة تقع مدافن شمل وضاية على مسافة قريبة من جبل يقدّم أنواعًا كثيرة من الصخر. فإذا اختار البناؤون صخورًا دون غيرها، وإذا اختار بناة وادي سوق غير ما اختاره بناة أم النار، فإن جدران المدافن ما زالت تحفظ تلك المعرفة.
وربما استعملوا ما كان أقرب إليهم، أو أخذوا حجارة من مدافن أقدم. وعدّ الصخور في جدران المدافن وفي الحصى الذي بجانبها عمل ميداني بسيط، يمكن أن يفرّق بين هذه القصص.

spec.te: Did the Sea Turn Sour Twice?
spec.desc: A connection between three records on this map, all in the Musandam mountains of Ras Al Khaimah within about 30 km of one another. At Wadi Bih, boron isotopes in shallow-marine carbonates record a pH fall of up to 0.7, lasting about 10,000 years, at the second pulse of the Permo-Triassic mass extinction about 252 million years ago; the authors link it to the preferential loss of heavily calcified marine life. At Wadi Naqab and Wadi Ghalilah, the Ghalilah Formation runs through the end-Triassic extinction about 201 million years ago; there one study found no clear evidence of a biocalcification crisis, and another reads the data as aragonite supersaturation rather than acidification. The records do not report boron isotopes from the Triassic–Jurassic sections. The idea: the contrast is real, and the boron method that found acidification at Wadi Bih will find no comparable pH fall across the Triassic–Jurassic boundary at Wadi Naqab and Wadi Ghalilah, so that these mountains hold one extinction driven partly by a souring sea and one that, at least on this shallow equatorial ramp, was not.
spec.sig: If true, a single mountain range would allow a side-by-side test of how two mass extinctions worked in the same region, and would show that acidification was decisive in one but not, or not everywhere, in the other. If false, the lack of a calcification crisis at the Triassic–Jurassic boundary would need another explanation.
spec.ev: Wadi Bih record: shallow-marine carbonate platform connected to the Neo-Tethys; boron isotopes stepped up from about 10.9‰ to 15.3‰ at about 252.04 Ma, then fell to about 8.2‰, calculated as a pH drop of up to 0.7; the acidification began near 251.88 Ma, lasted about 10,000 years and coincides with the second extinction pulse (Clarkson et al. 2015). Wadi Naqab record: equatorial mixed carbonate–siliciclastic ramp; Triassic–Jurassic boundary placed at the Shuba–Musandam transition (about 201.3 Ma); a tentative positive carbon-isotope shift of about 3.5–4‰; no clear evidence of a biocalcification crisis (Hönig et al. 2017). Wadi Ghalilah record: a complete, continuous shallow-water carbonate sequence from the Upper Triassic into the Lower Jurassic; a negative carbon-isotope excursion to about –2.8‰ just below the boundary; data pointing to aragonite supersaturation rather than acidification (Al-Suwaidi et al. 2016). Map distances: Wadi Bih to Wadi Naqab about 14 km, to Wadi Ghalilah about 15 km.
spec.an: Hönisch, Ridgwell, Schmidt and colleagues (2012) reviewed the geological record of ocean acidification and argued that the rate of carbon release, not only its amount, decides whether a past event left a true acidification signal, so that each candidate event has to be tested on its own evidence (Science 335, 1058–1063).
spec.val: Measure boron isotopes on well-preserved carbonate across the Shuba–Musandam transition at Wadi Naqab and the equivalent level at Wadi Ghalilah, with the approach used at Wadi Bih; screen every sample for later alteration; tie the samples to the carbon-isotope shifts already reported; compare the size and duration of any pH change with the Wadi Bih event; and compare the losses of heavily calcified fossils at the two boundaries.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: a real acidification pulse at the Triassic–Jurassic boundary was too short, or fell in too thin an interval, to be caught in the logged sections, so the contrast is a sampling artefact.
Rival explanation 2: local water chemistry on the equatorial ramp buffered a global acidification that struck elsewhere, so these sections say little about the open ocean.
Rival explanation 3: later alteration of the rocks has reset the boron signal, so neither the presence nor the absence of a pH fall can be read reliably.
refs: Clarkson, M.O., Kasemann, S.A., Wood, R.A., Lenton, T.M., Daines, S.J., Richoz, S., Ohnemueller, F., Meixner, A., Poulton, S.W. & Tipper, E.T. (2015). Ocean acidification and the Permo-Triassic mass extinction. Science 348(6231), 229–232.

spec.se: In the mountains of Ras Al Khaimah, rocks 252 million years old record a sea that turned more acidic during the worst extinction in Earth’s history; rocks 201 million years old, about 15 km away, show no clear sign of the same in a later mass extinction. Is the difference real? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: في جبال رأس الخيمة تحفظ صخور عمرها 252 مليون سنة بحرًا ازدادت حموضته في أثناء أسوأ انقراض عرفته الأرض، أما صخور عمرها 201 مليون سنة على بعد نحو 15 كيلومترًا فلا تُظهر علامة واضحة على ذلك في انقراض جماعي لاحق. فهل الفرق حقيقي؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from a coincidence of places on this map. Three geological records lie within about 30 km in the Musandam mountains of Ras Al Khaimah. The Wadi Bih record measures a pH fall at the end of the Permian; the Wadi Naqab and Wadi Ghalilah records cross the end of the Triassic and report no clear calcification crisis. The records do not report the two boundaries measured in the same way.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من تطابق أماكن على هذه الخريطة. ثلاثة سجلات جيولوجية تقع في نطاق نحو 30 كيلومترًا في جبال مسندم برأس الخيمة. يقيس سجل وادي البيح هبوطًا في الأس الهيدروجيني عند نهاية العصر البرمي، ويعبر سجلا وادي النقب ووادي غليلة نهاية العصر الترياسي دون أن يرصدا أزمة تكلّس واضحة. ولا تذكر هذه السجلات أن الحدّين قيسا بالطريقة نفسها.

title.en: The Mountain That Remembers Two Extinctions

tag.en: Rocks about 15 km apart in Ras Al Khaimah record two mass extinctions that may have worked in different ways
tag.ar: صخور تفصل بينها 15 كيلومترًا تقريبًا في رأس الخيمة تسجّل انقراضين جماعيين ربما اختلفت طريقة حدوثهما

en: High in the mountains of Ras Al Khaimah, the rocks of Wadi Bih were once the floor of a shallow sea. Hidden in them is a chemical clue, boron, which shows that about 252 million years ago the sea became more acidic for about 10,000 years, during the worst extinction in Earth’s history. Sea creatures with heavy shells and skeletons were hit hardest.

Only about 15 km away, at Wadi Naqab and Wadi Ghalilah, younger rocks from a warm sea near the equator run straight through another mass extinction, about 201 million years ago. The scientists who studied them found no clear sign that shell-builders were in trouble there.
ar: في أعالي جبال رأس الخيمة كانت صخور وادي البيح يومًا قاعَ بحرٍ ضحل. وفيها دليل كيميائي خفي، هو عنصر البورون، يكشف أن البحر ازداد حموضة قبل نحو 252 مليون سنة مدة 10,000 سنة تقريبًا، في أثناء أسوأ انقراض في تاريخ الأرض. وكانت الكائنات البحرية ذات الأصداف والهياكل الثقيلة أشدّ ما أصابه الضرر.

وعلى بعد نحو 15 كيلومترًا فقط، في وادي النقب ووادي غليلة، تمتد صخور أحدث عهدًا من بحر دافئ قرب خط الاستواء عبر انقراض جماعي آخر وقع قبل نحو 201 مليون سنة. ولم يجد العلماء الذين درسوها علامة واضحة على أن بُناة الأصداف كانوا في محنة هناك.

h2.en: Seen before: reading the sea’s chemistry in stone
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: قراءة كيمياء البحر في الحجر

en: In 2012 a large team of scientists led by Bärbel Hönisch looked back through the rock record for times when the oceans may have turned acidic.

Their lesson was simple: what matters is not only how much carbon enters the sea, but how fast. Each event in the past has to be tested on its own, because events that look alike may have worked very differently.
ar: في عام 2012 راجع فريق كبير من العلماء بقيادة بيربل هونيش سجل الصخور بحثًا عن أزمنة ربما صارت فيها المحيطات حمضية.
وكان درسهم بسيطًا: لا يهم مقدار الكربون الذي يدخل البحر فحسب، بل سرعة دخوله أيضًا. ولا بد من اختبار كل حدث قديم على حدة، لأن أحداثًا تبدو متشابهة ربما جرت بطرق مختلفة تمامًا.

en: On this map, two extinctions sit side by side in the same mountains. For one, the sea’s chemistry is known; for the other, the same clue has not yet been read. If the same test is used on both, we will learn whether the sea turned sour twice, or only once.
Perhaps a short pulse of acid at the younger boundary was simply missed. Or perhaps the warm equatorial sea protected its shell-builders. The rocks are waiting to be sampled.
ar: على هذه الخريطة يقف انقراضان جنبًا إلى جنب في الجبال نفسها. في أحدهما نعرف كيمياء البحر، وفي الآخر لم يُقرأ الدليل نفسه بعد. وإذا طُبّق الاختبار نفسه على الاثنين عرفنا هل صار البحر حمضيًا مرتين أم مرة واحدة.
ربما فاتت العلماءَ نبضةٌ حمضية قصيرة عند الحد الأحدث، وربما حمى البحرُ الاستوائي الدافئ بُناةَ أصدافه. والصخور تنتظر من يأخذ منها العينات.

spec.n: The Seam Between Two Ocean Blocks
spec.na: الدَّرز بين كتلتين من قاع المحيط
spec.te: Is Wadi Ham as Old as the Last Magmas?
spec.ta: هل وادي حام قديم قِدم آخر الصهارات؟
spec.desc: A connection between four records on this map in the Fujairah part of the Semail ophiolite. The Wadi Ham Fault Zone, on the route from Masafi to Fujairah, was mapped by the British Geological Survey as a north-west to south-east fault zone that separates the Khor Fakkan and Aswad ophiolite blocks; the sources do not date the faulting. The Masafi metamorphic window, the largest exposure of the ophiolite’s metamorphic sole in the UAE, also separates the two blocks and gives a rutile age of 94.1 ± 2.6 Ma. About 5 km from Al Bithnah, mingled gabbro and tonalite of the Fujairah facies belong to a later magmatic sequence of about 96.40–95.26 Ma, and the Aswad block holds the most extensive network of younger gabbros in the UAE ophiolite; at Ras Dadnah, further north, leucogranite and tonalite dykes cutting the mantle are dated about 92.4–91.0 Ma. The idea: the boundary that Wadi Ham follows did not first break long after the ophiolite formed, but was already a zone of weakness during the late magmatism and the start of thrusting, about 96–91 Ma, and helped guide where late magma rose.
spec.sig: If true, one of the main valleys and passes through the Hajar Mountains of the UAE would follow a structure as old as the ophiolite’s last magmas, and the division of the ophiolite into blocks would be part of how it was built and moved, not only a later overprint.
spec.ev: Wadi Ham Fault Zone record: NW–SE fault zone bounding the southern side of the Khor Fakkan block and separating it from the Aswad block; the Aswad block is about 70 km north–south and holds the most extensive network of younger gabbros; layered gabbros near Bithnah are mostly horizontal to gently inclined; the faulting is undated, and the record’s 96.4 Ma start is a broad estimate. Masafi record: about 100 km² of metamorphic sole; rutile age 94.1 ± 2.6 Ma; garnet–diopside amphibolites at about 800 ± 100 °C and 1.1 ± 0.2 GPa; the window separates the Khor Fakkan and Aswad blocks. Fujairah gabbro–tonalite record: felsic part dated 95.26 ± 0.31 Ma; later magmatic sequence about 96.40–95.26 Ma; obduction began around 94.5 Ma (Goodenough et al. 2010). Ras Dadnah record: leucogranite 92.361 ± 0.026 Ma, tonalites 91.292 ± 0.061 Ma and 90.998 ± 0.052 Ma, intruding mantle rocks (Rioux et al. 2021). Map distances from Al Bithnah: about 5 km to the dated Fujairah intrusion, about 16 km to Masafi and about 39 km to Ras Dadnah; the Al Bithnah, Masafi and Ras Dadnah points are village or town positions, not outcrops.
spec.an: van der Pluijm, Hall, Vrolijk, Pevear and Covey (2001) showed that clay minerals that grow inside fault rocks during movement can be dated, giving ages for faults that otherwise have no direct date (Nature 412, 172–175).
spec.val: Map the orientation of late gabbro, tonalite and granite dykes and sills against the NW–SE trend of the Wadi Ham Fault Zone; look for dykes that are deformed along the fault and for others that cut across it; date minerals grown in the fault rocks along Wadi Ham; compare the ages of the metamorphic sole and of the late intrusions on both sides of the fault.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the fault zone formed much later, during the uplift of the Hajar Mountains, and its position next to the late intrusions is a coincidence.
Rival explanation 2: the block boundary reflects how the ocean crust was built in separate segments, and the fault simply reused that boundary much later without moving at 96–91 Ma.
Rival explanation 3: the Masafi window was exposed by later folding and erosion, unrelated to any early movement along the Wadi Ham line.

Roberts, N.M.W., Thomas, R.J. & Jacobs, J. (2016). Geochronological constraints on the metamorphic sole of the Semail ophiolite in the United Arab Emirates. Geoscience Frontiers 7, 609–619.

Rioux, M., Garber, J.M., Searle, M., Kelemen, P., Miyashita, S., Adachi, Y. & Bowring, S. (2021). High-precision U-Pb zircon dating of late magmatism in the Samail ophiolite: A record of subduction initiation. Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth 126, e2020JB020758.
Heikal, M.T.S. (1999). Layering in gabbroid rocks from Semail ophiolite, United Arab Emirates: characterization, tectonic control on origin and orientation. JKAU: Earth Sciences 11, 33–58.
van der Pluijm, B.A., Hall, C.M., Vrolijk, P.J., Pevear, D.R. & Covey, M.C. (2001). The dating of shallow faults in the Earth’s crust. Nature 412, 172–175.
spec.se: Wadi Ham, an old route through the Hajar Mountains, follows a break between two giant blocks of ancient ocean floor. Around it, late magmas cooled 96 to 91 million years ago and the hot sole of the ophiolite lies exposed. Perhaps the break is as old as those magmas. Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: يسير وادي حام، الطريق القديم عبر جبال الحجر، على كسر بين كتلتين هائلتين من قاع محيط قديم. ومن حوله بردت صهارات متأخرة قبل 96 إلى 91 مليون سنة، وانكشف النعل الحار للأفيوليت. فلعل الكسر قديم قِدم تلك الصهارات. لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from a coincidence of places on this map. The Wadi Ham record describes an undated fault zone between the Khor Fakkan and Aswad blocks. The Masafi record describes the metamorphic sole exposed along the same boundary, and the Fujairah and Ras Dadnah records date late magmas within a few tens of kilometres. Three dated records cluster around one undated line.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من تطابق أماكن على هذه الخريطة. يصف سجل وادي حام نطاق صدع غير مؤرَّخ بين كتلتي خورفكان وأسود. ويصف سجل مسافي النعل المتحوّل منكشفًا على امتداد الحد نفسه، ويؤرّخ سجلا الفجيرة ورأس ضدنا صهارات متأخرة على بعد عشرات قليلة من الكيلومترات. ثلاثة سجلات مؤرَّخة تتجمع حول خط واحد بلا تاريخ.

tag.en: Wadi Ham may follow a crack as old as the last magmas of the ancient ocean floor
tag.ar: ربما يسير وادي حام على شقٍّ قديمٍ قِدمَ آخر الصهارات في قاع المحيط القديم

en: The mountains of Fujairah are made of old ocean floor that was pushed up onto the edge of Arabia. A great break runs along Wadi Ham and splits them into two giant blocks. People have long used the valley as a way through the mountains, but nobody knows when the break first formed.

Around it lie clues with dates: near Masafi, rocks that were baked under the sliding ocean floor about 94 million years ago; near Fujairah, dark and pale magmas that swirled together about 95 million years ago; and at Ras Dadnah, white granite veins about 92 to 91 million years old.
ar: جبال الفجيرة مصنوعة من قاع محيط قديم دُفع فوق حافة الجزيرة العربية. ويمتد على طول وادي حام كسر عظيم يقسمها إلى كتلتين هائلتين. وقد اتخذ الناس الوادي منذ زمن بعيد طريقًا عبر الجبال، لكن أحدًا لا يعرف متى تكوّن الكسر أول مرة.

ومن حوله تنتشر أدلة لها تواريخ: قرب مسافي صخور طُهيت تحت قاع المحيط الزاحف قبل نحو 94 مليون سنة، وقرب الفجيرة صهارتان داكنة وفاتحة امتزجتا قبل نحو 95 مليون سنة، وفي رأس ضدنا عروق من الجرانيت الأبيض عمرها نحو 92 إلى 91 مليون سنة.

h2.en: Seen before: putting a date on a fault

en: A fault is a crack in the Earth, and cracks are hard to date. In 2001 the geologist Ben van der Pluijm and his colleagues found a way: as rocks grind along a fault, tiny new clay crystals grow inside the crushed rock.
Those crystals carry their own clock. By dating them, the team could tell when faults had moved, even faults that had no other clue to their age.
ar: الصدع شق في الأرض، والشقوق يصعب تأريخها. وفي عام 2001 وجد الجيولوجي بن فان دير بلويم وزملاؤه طريقة لذلك: فحين تحتك الصخور على امتداد صدع تنمو بلورات طينية جديدة دقيقة داخل الصخر المسحوق.
وتحمل هذه البلورات ساعتها الخاصة. وبتأريخها استطاع الفريق أن يعرف متى تحركت الصدوع، حتى تلك التي لا دليل آخر على عمرها.

en: On this map, three dated places cluster around one undated line. If the break along Wadi Ham was already there while the last magmas rose, some granite and gabbro veins will bend along it, and crystals in its crushed rock will be very old.
If the break came much later, every vein will simply be cut through, and the crystals will be young. A geologist with a hammer, a map and a laboratory could begin to tell which.
ar: على هذه الخريطة تتجمع ثلاثة أماكن مؤرَّخة حول خط واحد بلا تاريخ. فإن كان الكسر على طول وادي حام موجودًا حين صعدت آخر الصهارات، فستنثني بعض عروق الجرانيت والغابرو على امتداده، وستكون البلورات في صخره المسحوق قديمة جدًا.
وإن جاء الكسر بعد ذلك بزمن طويل، فستكون كل العروق مقطوعة ببساطة، وستكون البلورات حديثة. وجيولوجي معه مطرقة وخريطة ومختبر يستطيع أن يبدأ في التمييز بين الاحتمالين.

spec.n: The Fort the Creek Left Behind
spec.te: Did Mud Close the Portuguese Fort at Kalba?
spec.ta: هل أغلق الطمي الحصن البرتغالي في كلباء؟
spec.desc: A connection between four records on this map along the Sea of Oman coast of Sharjah. The Portuguese rammed-earth fort at the mouth of the Khor Kalba tidal creek, seized in 1624 and used as a navigation aid, trading station and supply depot, was probably abandoned in the 18th century, possibly as the creek silted; a later Qasimi fort stands to the north-east. About 3 km to the south, the Khor Kalba mangroves hold the tallest and most extensive mature mangrove woodland in the region, among tidal channels, salt marsh and beach. Further north, the forts of Khor Fakkan, on a sheltered bay, and Dibba Al-Hisn, on Dibba Bay, have records of use continuing into the 19th and 20th centuries. The idea: the silting suggested in the Khor Kalba fort record really happened, at the time the fort was given up, and it is written in the sediments of the creek and its mangrove fringe, while the open bays to the north show no matching infill in the same period.
spec.sig: If true, the end of the Portuguese supply station at Kalba would be partly an environmental story, and the mud of the mangrove creek could date changes along this coast that written sources record only vaguely.
spec.ev: Khor Kalba fort record: southern component of the Coastal Fortified Network of South Eastern Arabia (UNESCO Tentative List, 2026); at the mouth of the Khor Kalba tidal creek and mangrove lagoon; seized by Portuguese forces in 1624; rammed earth on stone foundations; a quadrangular enclosure with two circular corner towers; probably abandoned in the 18th century, possibly as the creek silted; a later fort to the north-east reflects Al Qasimi consolidation in the 18th and 19th centuries. Khor Kalba mangrove record: 1,494 ha Ramsar site; the tallest and most extensive mature Avicennia marina woodland in the biogeographic region; tidal channels, salt marsh and beach. Khor Fakkan record: a sheltered crescent bay; a Portuguese fort built in 1620; West Fort phases from the 17th to the 19th century. Dibba Al-Hisn record: on Dibba Bay; a sequence from the Neolithic to the 20th century; a governor’s residence in the 19th and 20th centuries. Map distances: fort to the mangrove marker about 3 km; Kalba fort to Khor Fakkan about 36 km and to Dibba about 66 km.
spec.an: Marriner and Morhange (2007) reviewed the geoscience of ancient Mediterranean harbours and showed that harbour basins act as sediment traps whose layers record the building, use, silting and abandonment of a port, so that its history can be read from its mud (Earth-Science Reviews 80, 137–194).
spec.val: Core the creek bed and mangrove fringe beside the Portuguese and Qasimi forts; date the layers; look for a change from coarse channel sediment to fine silt or mangrove mud; compare the dates with the building and abandonment phases of the two forts; take matching cores in the bays of Khor Fakkan and Dibba as controls.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the Portuguese station was given up for political or military reasons, and any silting came later or played no part.
Rival explanation 2: the later fort was placed to the north-east for defence or to serve a new settlement, not because the old channel had closed.
Rival explanation 3: the creek filled gradually over a much longer time with no particular change in the 17th–18th centuries, so its sediments cannot explain the timing of the abandonment.
refs: UNESCO World Heritage Centre (2026). Coastal Fortified Network of South Eastern Arabia, Tentative List ref. 7039 (submitted 28/07/2026).

spec.se: A Portuguese fort at the mouth of the Khor Kalba creek was probably abandoned in the 18th century, possibly as the creek silted. The mud of the mangrove creek beside it could show whether that is true. Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: هُجر حصن برتغالي عند مصب خور كلباء في القرن الثامن عشر على الأرجح، وربما كان السبب ترسّب الطمي في الخور. وطمي خور القرم المجاور قد يكشف إن كان ذلك صحيحًا. لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from one phrase in a record. The Khor Kalba fort record says the fort was abandoned possibly as the creek silted. The Khor Kalba mangrove record, about 3 km away, describes the tidal channels and salt marsh where that silt would lie. The forts of Khor Fakkan and Dibba, on open bays to the north, offer a comparison.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من عبارة واحدة في سجل. يقول سجل حصن خور كلباء إن الحصن هُجر ربما بسبب ترسّب الطمي في الخور. ويصف سجل قرم خور كلباء، على بعد نحو 3 كيلومترات، القنوات المدّية والسبخات الملحية التي يُفترض أن يستقر فيها ذلك الطمي. أما حصنا خورفكان ودبا، على خليجين مفتوحين إلى الشمال، فيقدّمان أساسًا للمقارنة.

title.en: The Fort and the Muddy Creek

tag.en: Mangrove mud at Kalba may explain why a Portuguese fort was left empty
tag.ar: قد يفسّر طمي القرم في كلباء لماذا تُرك حصن برتغالي خاليًا

en: In 1624 Portuguese forces took a fortified settlement at the mouth of the Khor Kalba creek. They built a fort of rammed earth on stone footings, with two round towers, and used it to guide ships, trade and store supplies.

By the 18th century the fort was probably empty, and the archaeologists think the creek may have filled with silt. A short way south, the creek winds into the tallest mangrove forest in the region, where tidal channels slowly gather mud.
ar: في عام 1624 استولت القوات البرتغالية على مستوطنة محصنة عند مصب خور كلباء. وبنت حصنًا من التراب المدكوك على أساسات حجرية، له برجان مستديران، واستعملته لإرشاد السفن وللتجارة وتخزين المؤن.

وبحلول القرن الثامن عشر كان الحصن قد خلا على الأرجح، ويرى علماء الآثار أن الخور ربما امتلأ بالطمي. وعلى مسافة قصيرة جنوبًا يتعرّج الخور داخل أطول غابة قرم في المنطقة، حيث تجمع القنوات المدّية الطين ببطء.

h2.en: Seen before: harbours that filled with mud
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: موانئ امتلأت بالطمي

en: Around the Mediterranean, many ancient harbours now lie inland, under fields and towns. In 2007 the scientists Nick Marriner and Christophe Morhange brought together the evidence from many of these lost ports.
They showed that a harbour is a trap for mud. Layer by layer, its sediments record when it was built, used, choked and abandoned, like the pages of a history book.
ar: حول البحر المتوسط تقع اليوم موانئ قديمة كثيرة في البر، تحت الحقول والمدن. وفي عام 2007 جمع العالمان نِك مارينر وكريستوف مورانج أدلة من موانئ مفقودة كثيرة.
وبيّنا أن الميناء مصيدة للطمي. فطبقةً بعد طبقة تسجّل رواسبه متى بُني واستُعمل واختنق وهُجر، كأنها صفحات كتاب تاريخ.

en: On this map, a fort that may have been lost to silt stands beside a mangrove creek full of mud. If the creek closed in the 1600s or 1700s, cores drilled into its bed will show the change, and the forts on the open bays of Khor Fakkan and Dibba, used into later centuries, will show nothing like it.
But perhaps the Portuguese left for other reasons, and the mud came later. The mud itself can be dated.
ar: على هذه الخريطة يقف حصن ربما خسره أصحابه بسبب الطمي إلى جوار خور قرم مليء بالطين. فإن كان الخور قد انسدّ في القرن السابع عشر أو الثامن عشر، فستكشف العينات المأخوذة من قاعه هذا التغير، ولن يظهر شيء مثله عند الحصنين المطلين على خليجي خورفكان ودبا المفتوحين، وقد ظلا مستعملين قرونًا بعده.
لكن ربما رحل البرتغاليون لأسباب أخرى، وجاء الطمي لاحقًا. والطمي نفسه يمكن تأريخه.

spec.n: The Dugong Mound and the High Sea
spec.te: Did a Higher Sea Bring the Dugongs to Akab?
spec.ta: هل جلب البحر المرتفع الأطوم إلى عكاب؟
spec.desc: A connection between four records on this map. On Akab, a small island in Khor al-Beidah, the lagoon of Umm Al Quwain, a Late Neolithic settlement is dated by radiocarbon to about 4748–3814 BC, and a ritual mound holding more than 40 dugongs to 3522–3226 BC. The record of the Umm Al Quwain spit, about 3 km away, says sea level stood about 2 m higher than today around 5,500 BP and about 1.5 m higher around 4,500 BP, and that the lagoon reached its greatest extent only around 3,500 BP. Today Khor Al Beidah is a tidal wetland of mudflats, sandflats and mangrove, and the dugongs of the UAE live mainly on shallow seagrass banks west of Abu Dhabi, around Marawah and Bu Tinah, about 270 km away. The idea: the dugong mound was built when the higher sea of the mid-Holocene brought seagrass, and with it dugongs, within reach of Akab, so that the ritual reflects a local hunting ground that changed as the sea fell and the spit grew.
spec.sig: If true, the oldest known ritual site associated with the dugong would be tied to a particular moment of high sea and to seagrass close to shore, and the Umm Al Quwain lagoon would become a case of a shifting coastline shaping how people used the sea.
spec.ev: Akab record: island in Khor al-Beidah, found in 1989 and excavated again in 2006–2008; Late Neolithic settlement c. 4748–3814 BC; ovoid mound of about 10 m², 0.30–0.40 m high, with the remains of more than 40 dugongs, mandibles forming a base and skulls in aligned rows, and several hundred objects such as shell and soft-stone beads; mound dated 3522–3226 BC (2σ); fish bones of 56 bony-fish species in 42 genera and 22 families (Méry et al. 2009; Lidour et al. 2019). Umm Al Quwain spit record: lagoon about 20 km long, 8 km wide and about 127 km²; sea level about 2 m higher around 5,500 BP and about 1.5 m higher around 4,500 BP; lagoon at its maximum extent around 3,500 BP; southern ridge breached around 2,600 BP; lagoon nearly closed by about 1,500 BP (Bernier et al. 1995, as summarised by Forti et al. 2024). Khor Al Beidah record: today mudflats, sandflats and mangrove. Marawah and Bu Tinah record: about 3,000 dugongs in Abu Dhabi waters, on shallow seagrass banks west of Abu Dhabi. Map distances: Akab to the spit marker about 3 km; Akab to Bu Tinah about 270 km.
spec.an: McNiven and Feldman (2003) studied dugong bone mounds built by Torres Strait Islanders in north-eastern Australia and interpreted them as ritual structures linked to hunting magic and to the stretches of sea where dugongs were hunted (Cambridge Archaeological Journal 13, 169–194).
spec.val: Core the lagoon floor and the old shorelines around Akab for seagrass indicators such as seagrass-dwelling shells and foraminifera, and date them; check whether they peak at the time of the mound; sort the 56 fish species already identified at Akab by habitat and compare the share of seagrass species layer by layer; date dugong bones from all layers of the site and compare their abundance with the sea-level curve.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the dugongs were hunted far out in the open Arabian Gulf and brought to Akab for the ritual, so seagrass in the lagoon does not matter.
Rival explanation 2: Akab was chosen as a ritual place for reasons such as visibility or the island’s meaning, and the match with the high sea level is a coincidence of dates.
Rival explanation 3: the uncertainties in dating marine bone and shell are too large to tie the mound to a particular sea level at all.
refs: Méry, S., Charpentier, V., Auxiette, G. & Pelle, E. (2009). A dugong bone mound: the Neolithic ritual site on Akab in Umm al-Quwain, United Arab Emirates. Antiquity 83, 696–708.

Lidour, K., Béarez, P., Charpentier, V. & Méry, S. (2019). The Prehistoric Fisheries of Akab Island (United Arab Emirates): New Insights into Coastal Subsistence during Neolithic in Eastern Arabia. The Journal of Island and Coastal Archaeology.

Forti, L., Degli Esposti, M., Cremaschi, M., Borgi, F., Azzoni, R.S. & Zerboni, A. (2024). Geomorphological evolution of the Umm al-Quwain (UAE) coastal-lagoon system: Natural processes and recent human impact. Catena 247, 108517.
BirdLife International (2017). Important Bird Area factsheet: Khor Al Beidah, United Arab Emirates.
Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi. Dugong (Dugong dugon) species page.
McNiven, I.J. & Feldman, R. (2003). Ritually orchestrated seascapes: hunting magic and dugong bone mounds in Torres Strait, NE Australia. Cambridge Archaeological Journal 13(2), 169–194.
spec.se: On a small island in the lagoon of Umm Al Quwain, people laid the skulls of more than 40 dugongs in rows more than 5,000 years ago, when the sea stood higher than today. Did the high sea bring seagrass and dugongs close to the island? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: على جزيرة صغيرة في خور أم القيوين صفّ الناس جماجم أكثر من 40 أطومًا في صفوف قبل أكثر من 5,000 عام، حين كان البحر أعلى مما هو اليوم. فهل جلب البحر المرتفع الأعشابَ البحرية والأطومَ قريبًا من الجزيرة؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from two records side by side. The Akab record dates a mound of more than 40 dugongs to 3522–3226 BC. The record of the Umm Al Quwain spit, about 3 km away, says the sea then stood up to about 2 m higher than today. Neither record asks whether the two are linked.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من سجلين متجاورين. يؤرّخ سجل عكاب ركامًا لأكثر من 40 أطومًا بين 3522 و3226 ق.م. ويقول سجل لسان أم القيوين، على بعد نحو 3 كيلومترات، إن البحر كان آنذاك أعلى مما هو اليوم بنحو مترين. ولا يسأل أي من السجلين عن صلة بين الأمرين.

tag.en: A higher sea may have brought dugongs to a small island in Umm Al Quwain
tag.ar: ربما جلب بحرٌ أعلى الأطومَ إلى جزيرة صغيرة في أم القيوين

en: On Akab, a small island in the lagoon of Umm Al Quwain, Neolithic people built a low mound of dugong bones between 3522 and 3226 BC. They laid the jaws as a base and set the skulls of more than 40 dugongs in neat rows, with hundreds of beads and other objects.
At that time the sea was higher than it is today, by about 2 m around 5,500 years ago. The long sand spit and the lagoon we see now were still taking shape.
ar: على عكاب، الجزيرة الصغيرة في خور أم القيوين، بنى أناس من العصر الحجري الحديث ركامًا منخفضًا من عظام الأطوم بين 3522 و3226 ق.م. وضعوا الفكوك قاعدةً، وصفّوا فوقها جماجم أكثر من 40 أطومًا في صفوف منتظمة، ومعها مئات الخرز وأشياء أخرى.
وكان البحر آنذاك أعلى مما هو اليوم، بنحو مترين قبل نحو 5,500 عام. وكان اللسان الرملي الطويل والخور اللذان نراهما الآن لا يزالان في طور التشكّل.

h2.en: Seen before: the bone mounds of Torres Strait
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: ركامات العظام في مضيق توريس

en: Between Australia and New Guinea lie the islands of Torres Strait, where people have hunted dugongs for a very long time. There, too, hunters built mounds of dugong bones.
In 2003 the archaeologists McNiven and Feldman studied these mounds and argued that they were part of hunting magic: ritual places tied to the stretches of sea where the dugongs were caught.
ar: بين أستراليا وغينيا الجديدة تقع جزر مضيق توريس، حيث يصطاد الناس الأطوم منذ زمن بعيد جدًا. وهناك أيضًا بنى الصيادون ركامات من عظام الأطوم.
وفي عام 2003 درس عالما الآثار ماكنيفن وفيلدمان هذه الركامات، ورأيا أنها جزء من سحر الصيد: أماكن طقسية مرتبطة بمساحات البحر التي كان الأطوم يُصاد فيها.

en: On this map, the dugong mound and the high sea fall at the same time. Perhaps seagrass grew close to Akab when the water was deeper, and dugongs came to graze within reach of the island.
Or perhaps the hunters went far out to sea and brought the bones home for the ritual. Mud from the lagoon floor, full of tiny shells, could show whether seagrass grew there then.
ar: على هذه الخريطة يقع ركام الأطوم والبحر المرتفع في الزمن نفسه. فربما نمت الأعشاب البحرية قرب عكاب حين كان الماء أعمق، وجاء الأطوم يرعى على مقربة من الجزيرة.
أو ربما أبحر الصيادون بعيدًا وعادوا بالعظام لأداء الطقس. وطين قاع الخور، المليء بالأصداف الدقيقة، قد يكشف إن كانت الأعشاب البحرية تنمو هناك آنذاك.

spec.n: The Last Wild Asses of the Kalba Valleys
spec.na: آخر الحمير البرية في أودية كلباء
spec.te: When Did the Wild Ass Leave the Hajar?
spec.ta: متى غاب الحمار البري عن جبال الحجر؟
spec.dr: c. 5th millennium BC – 2nd millennium BC (test window)
spec.desc: A connection between three records on this map. At Khatm Al-Melaha near Kalba, the first rock art site found in the Hajar Mountains, the oldest phase of pictures, around the 5th millennium BCE, shows wild asses, probably the extinct Syrian wild ass; they are overlain by 4th-millennium BCE ibex or wild goats and then by abstract designs and human figures of the 3rd–2nd millennium BCE and later. About 13 km to the west, the Bronze Age copper valley of Wadi Al Helo also has rock art with Syrian wild asses, alongside T-shaped figures and boats, but no dates are given for them. Its dossier links the valley to Bronze Age centres such as Tell Abraq, where more than 100,000 animal bones were collected from layers dated from about 2200 BC to AD 200. The idea: the wild ass had already vanished from these valleys before the Bronze Age copper workers arrived, so the wild-ass pictures of Wadi Al Helo belong to the same early phase as those of Khatm Al-Melaha and are older than the boats and T-shaped figures.
spec.sig: If true, the rock art of the two valleys would record the disappearance of a large wild animal from south-eastern Arabia, and it would give a way to date the undated pictures of Wadi Al Helo by comparing them with Khatm Al-Melaha.
spec.ev: Khatm Al-Melaha record: first rock art site discovered in the Hajar Mountains; component of The Rock Art of the Emirate of Sharjah on the UNESCO Tentative List (2023); three superimposed phases: wild asses, probably the extinct Syrian wild ass (Equus hemionus hemippus), around the 5th millennium BCE; ibex or wild goats of the 4th millennium BCE in the three-strokes style laid over them; abstract designs and human figures of the 3rd–2nd millennium BCE and later. Wadi Al Helo record: valley of about 84 km² with Bronze Age copper mining and smelting in open workings in the ophiolite, hilltop furnaces, slag heaps, workshops, a casting pit and a watchtower; rock art with T-shaped figures, boats and Syrian wild asses; the source gives no dates; the dossier links it to Tell Abraq, Kalba and Umm an-Nar. Tell Abraq record: occupation from about 2200 BC to AD 200; more than 100,000 animal bones, the largest faunal assemblage in the Arabian Peninsula. Map distances: Khatm Al-Melaha to Wadi Al Helo about 13 km; Wadi Al Helo to Tell Abraq about 87 km.
spec.an: In rock art studies the relative order of pictures is usually read from superimposition, which image was cut over which, and from differences in weathering and the dark patina that grows on rock surfaces over time; this is how the three phases at Khatm Al-Melaha were separated. In many desert regions, changes in the animals shown from one phase to the next have also been used as a record of changing wildlife. No single published case is cited here.
spec.val: Record every wild-ass, boat and T-shaped figure at Wadi Al Helo and note which pictures overlie which; measure the weathering and patina of each against the dated phases at Khatm Al-Melaha; check whether any wild ass is pecked on stones belonging to the copper workings; identify any wild equid bones among the Tell Abraq animal bones and see in which layers they occur.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the wild ass survived into the Bronze Age, and the copper workers themselves drew the wild asses at Wadi Al Helo.
Rival explanation 2: the pictures of the two valleys belong to different traditions, so the dates of Khatm Al-Melaha say nothing about Wadi Al Helo.
Rival explanation 3: differences in patina come from different kinds of rock and exposure, not from age, so the pictures cannot be ordered this way.

spec.se: Near Kalba, people carved wild asses that no longer exist about 7,000 years ago, and the copper valley of Wadi Al Helo, 13 km away, has wild asses too. Were they drawn before the copper workers came? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: قرب كلباء نقش الناس قبل نحو 7,000 عام حميرًا برية لم تعد موجودة، وفي وادي الحلو للنحاس، على بعد 13 كيلومترًا، حمير برية أيضًا. فهل رُسمت قبل مجيء عمّال النحاس؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from one animal in two records. The Khatm Al-Melaha record dates its wild asses to around the 5th millennium BCE. The Wadi Al Helo record, about 13 km away, lists Syrian wild asses among its rock art but gives no date. The Tell Abraq record, with more than 100,000 animal bones, offers a way to check when the animal was still around.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من حيوان واحد في سجلين. يؤرّخ سجل ختم الملاحة حميره البرية بنحو الألفية الخامسة قبل الميلاد. ويذكر سجل وادي الحلو، على بعد نحو 13 كيلومترًا، حميرًا برية سورية بين نقوشه الصخرية دون أن يحدد لها تاريخًا. أما سجل تل أبرق، بأكثر من 100,000 عظمة حيوانية، فيقدّم وسيلة للتحقق من الزمن الذي كان فيه هذا الحيوان لا يزال موجودًا.

title.en: The Donkey That Left the Mountains

tag.en: Pictures on the rocks near Kalba may show when a wild animal vanished
tag.ar: قد تكشف صور على صخور قرب كلباء متى اختفى حيوان بري

en: Near Kalba, on rocks of the Hajar Mountains, people carved wild asses around the 5th millennium BCE. They were probably Syrian wild asses, animals that are now extinct. Later artists carved ibex over them, and later still came abstract signs and human figures.

About 13 km away, in Wadi Al Helo, where Bronze Age people mined and smelted copper, the rocks also show wild asses, beside boats and T-shaped figures. But nobody has said how old those wild asses are.
ar: قرب كلباء، على صخور جبال الحجر، نقش الناس حميرًا برية في نحو الألفية الخامسة قبل الميلاد. وكانت على الأرجح حميرًا برية سورية، وهي حيوانات منقرضة اليوم. ثم نقش فنانون لاحقون وعولًا فوقها، وجاءت بعد ذلك رموز مجردة وأشكال بشرية.
وعلى بعد نحو 13 كيلومترًا، في وادي الحلو حيث استخرج أهل العصر البرونزي النحاس وصهروه، تظهر على الصخور حمير برية أيضًا، إلى جانب قوارب وأشكال على هيئة حرف T. لكن أحدًا لم يحدد عمر تلك الحمير.

h2.en: Seen before: reading pictures layer by layer
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: قراءة الصور طبقةً طبقة

en: Rock art experts often work like detectives. When one picture is cut over another, the one underneath must be older. And the longer a picture has been exposed to sun and weather, the darker the coating that grows over it.
This is how the three phases at Khatm Al-Melaha were told apart. In many deserts, the animals shown from one phase to the next have also been read as a record of the wildlife that came and went.
ar: كثيرًا ما يعمل خبراء الفنون الصخرية كالمحققين. فإذا نُقشت صورة فوق أخرى، فالتي في الأسفل أقدم لا محالة. وكلما طال تعرّض الصورة للشمس وتقلبات الطقس، اشتدّت عتمة الطبقة التي تغطيها.
وبهذه الطريقة مُيّزت المراحل الثلاث في ختم الملاحة. وفي صحارى كثيرة قُرئت الحيوانات المصوّرة من مرحلة إلى أخرى سجلًّا للحياة البرية التي جاءت ثم رحلت.

en: On this map, the same lost animal appears in two valleys 13 km apart. If it had already vanished before the copper workers came, the wild asses of Wadi Al Helo will lie under the boats, look as weathered as the oldest pictures at Khatm Al-Melaha, and be missing from the Bronze Age bones of Tell Abraq.
But perhaps the copper workers still saw wild asses and drew them. Then the pictures, and the bones, will tell a different story.
ar: على هذه الخريطة يظهر الحيوان المفقود نفسه في واديين يفصل بينهما 13 كيلومترًا. فإن كان قد اختفى قبل مجيء عمّال النحاس، فستكون حمير وادي الحلو تحت القوارب، وستبدو متآكلة كأقدم صور ختم الملاحة، وستغيب عن عظام العصر البرونزي في تل أبرق.
لكن ربما كان عمّال النحاس لا يزالون يرون الحمير البرية فرسموها. وعندها ستروي الصور والعظام قصة أخرى.
