spec.te: Does a Far Island Re-Seed the Coastal Reefs?
spec.ta: هل تزرع جزيرة بعيدة الشعاب الساحلية من جديد؟
spec.desc: A connection between three records on this map in the Arabian Gulf waters of Abu Dhabi and Sharjah. Sir Bu Nair is an offshore island about 110 km from Sharjah, formed by a salt dome, with 40 coral and 76 reef fish species recorded by Ramsar. Ras Ghanada, about 64 km to the south-east near Ghantoot, is the largest reef on the Arabian Gulf side of the UAE and holds about 40% of the coral species of the Arabian Gulf, after the 1996–98 El Niño killed about 90% of Gulf corals; it lies close to the breakwater of Khalifa Port. Al Saadiyat Marine National Park, about 46 km from Ras Ghanada, includes about 7 km² of coral reefs beside the city of Abu Dhabi. The idea: the reefs around the far, undeveloped salt-dome island act as a nursery whose coral larvae drift to the coastal reefs and help them recover after mass bleaching.
spec.sig: If true, protecting a remote island would also protect the future of the reefs near the cities, and the reefs of the UAE would have to be managed as one connected network rather than as separate sites.
spec.ev: Sir Bu Nair record: offshore island about 110 km from Sharjah formed by a mineral-rich salt dome; protected by Decree No. 25 of 2000; Ramsar site no. 2191 (4,964 ha, of which 1,333 ha land); 40 coral and 76 reef fish species in the Ramsar summary (20 corals and 58 reef fish in the earlier UNESCO entry). Ras Ghanada record: near Ghantoot about 90 km north-east of Abu Dhabi city; the most extensive reef on the Arabian Gulf side of the UAE; monitored since 2010 with fish counts and seafloor photographs every three metres; the 1996–98 El Niño killed about 90% of Gulf corals; close to the breakwater of Khalifa Port, opened in 2012; protected area of 55 km² with about 40% of Arabian Gulf coral species. Al Saadiyat record: marine national park declared in 2017, 59 km², about 7 km² of coral reefs and 8 km² of seagrass. Map distances: Sir Bu Nair to Ras Ghanada about 64 km; Sir Bu Nair to Al Saadiyat about 66 km; Ras Ghanada to Al Saadiyat about 46 km.
spec.an: Hughes and colleagues (2019) showed on the Great Barrier Reef that after the mass bleaching of 2016 and 2017 the number of young corals settling on the reef fell steeply, because so many of the adult corals that supply larvae had died; the recovery of a reef depends on larvae from corals that survive elsewhere (Nature 568, 387–390).
spec.val: Sample a common reef-building coral at Sir Bu Nair, Ras Ghanada and Al Saadiyat and compare their genes to measure how much each population descends from the others; model the drift of coral larvae with the currents of the spawning season; set out settlement tiles on the coastal reefs and identify where the young corals come from.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the coastal reefs re-seed themselves from their own surviving colonies, and larvae from far away play almost no part.
Rival explanation 2: the larvae come mainly from other reefs, such as those around the western islands of Abu Dhabi, not from Sir Bu Nair.
Rival explanation 3: the coastal reefs recovered mostly by the regrowth of damaged colonies rather than by new larvae.

spec.se: Far out in the Arabian Gulf, the reefs of Sir Bu Nair hold 40 kinds of coral. Do their tiny larvae drift to the coast and help reefs like Ras Ghanada recover from heat? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: في عرض الخليج العربي تضم شعاب صير بونعير 40 نوعًا من المرجان. فهل تنجرف يرقاتها الدقيقة إلى الساحل وتساعد شعابًا مثل رأس غناضة على التعافي من الحرارة؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from three reefs on one map. The Ras Ghanada record says the 1996–98 El Niño killed about 90% of Gulf corals, yet the reef today holds about 40% of all Arabian Gulf coral species. The Sir Bu Nair record shows 40 coral species around a far island, about 64 km away. Al Saadiyat, near the city, has about 7 km² of coral reefs. Where did the new corals come from?
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من ثلاث شعاب على خريطة واحدة. يقول سجل رأس غناضة إن ظاهرة النينيو في 1996–1998 قتلت نحو 90% من مرجان الخليج، ومع ذلك تضم الشعاب اليوم نحو 40% من أنواع مرجان الخليج العربي كلها. ويُظهر سجل صير بونعير 40 نوعًا من المرجان حول جزيرة بعيدة، على بعد نحو 64 كيلومترًا. وفي السعديات، قرب المدينة، نحو 7 كيلومترات مربعة من الشعاب. فمن أين جاء المرجان الجديد؟

tag.en: A far island’s reefs may help the coral of Abu Dhabi grow back
tag.ar: ربما تساعد شعاب جزيرة بعيدة مرجان أبوظبي على النمو من جديد

en: In 1996–98 a great warming of the sea, linked to El Niño, killed about 90% of the corals of the Arabian Gulf. Yet today Ras Ghanada, near Ghantoot, is the largest reef on the Gulf side of the Emirates and holds about 40% of all the Gulf’s coral species.
Far out to sea, about 64 km away, lies Sir Bu Nair, an island raised by salt, with reefs of 40 coral species and no town or port beside them.
ar: في 1996–1998 قتل احترار كبير في البحر، مرتبط بظاهرة النينيو، نحو 90% من مرجان الخليج العربي. ومع ذلك فإن رأس غناضة، قرب غنتوت، هو اليوم أكبر شعاب على ساحل الخليج في الإمارات، ويضم نحو 40% من أنواع مرجان الخليج كلها.
وبعيدًا في البحر، على بعد نحو 64 كيلومترًا، تقع صير بونعير، الجزيرة التي رفعها الملح، وحولها شعاب فيها 40 نوعًا من المرجان، بلا مدينة ولا ميناء بجوارها.

h2.en: Seen before: the Great Barrier Reef
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: الحاجز المرجاني العظيم

en: In 2016 and 2017 the Great Barrier Reef of Australia suffered huge bleaching. Terry Hughes and his colleagues then counted the young corals settling on the reef in the years after.
They found far fewer than before, because so many parent corals had died. A reef can only grow back if baby corals arrive from corals that survived somewhere else.
ar: في عامَي 2016 و2017 أصاب ابيضاض هائل الحاجز المرجاني العظيم في أستراليا. ثم أحصى تيري هيوز وزملاؤه المرجانيات الصغيرة التي استقرت على الشعاب في السنوات التالية.
فوجدوها أقل بكثير من قبل، لأن عددًا كبيرًا من المرجانيات الأم كان قد مات. فالشعاب لا تعود إلى النمو إلا إذا وصلتها صغار مرجان من مرجانيات نجت في مكان آخر.

en: On this map, a far, quiet reef and two reefs beside a busy coast lie within about 66 km of each other. If Sir Bu Nair is their nursery, the corals of Ras Ghanada and Saadiyat will share its genes, and the currents will carry larvae towards the coast.
Or perhaps each coastal reef re-seeded itself from its own survivors. Coral genes can tell the difference.
ar: على هذه الخريطة تقع شعاب بعيدة هادئة وشعابان بجوار ساحل مزدحم، لا تزيد المسافة بينها على نحو 66 كيلومترًا. فإن كانت صير بونعير مشتلًا لها، فستشترك مرجانيات رأس غناضة والسعديات في جيناتها، وستحمل التيارات اليرقات نحو الساحل.
أو ربما زرعت كل شعاب ساحلية نفسها من جديد من مرجانياتها الناجية. وجينات المرجان قادرة على كشف الفرق.

spec.n: One Water for the Falaj and the Dragonflies
spec.te: Do the Falaj and the Wetland Drink from the Same Rock?
spec.ta: هل يشرب الفلج والأرض الرطبة من صخرة واحدة؟
spec.desc: A connection between two records on this map in the Hatta enclave of Dubai, about 5 km apart. The Hatta Archaeological Landscape has 22 mapped sites, among them the Jabal al Yamh necropolis with over 70 tombs, villages with agricultural terraces at Suhaila 2 and Wadi Jeema, and an underground falaj about 560 m long dated to the 1st millennium BCE. The Hatta Mountain Reserve, a Ramsar site in the Hajar Mountains on the Oman–UAE ophiolite, is a rare mountain freshwater ecosystem: these mountains receive about 30% of the country’s annual rainfall, which recharges the aquifer feeding the Hatta and Al Ghabra dams, and the reserve holds 79% of the country’s dragonfly species. The idea: the falaj builders and the wetland draw on one and the same groundwater stored in the fractured ophiolite, so that the places where people dug their channel and built their terraces are the places where this water comes closest to the surface.
spec.sig: If true, the falaj would be a marker, more than 2,000 years old, of where Hatta’s mountain water reaches the valley, and protecting that water would protect the heritage landscape and the wetland life of the reserve together.
spec.ev: Hatta Archaeological Landscape record: UNESCO Tentative List 2023; 22 archaeological sites identified, documented and mapped; Jabal al Yamh necropolis with over 70 tombs over about 4 km, mostly Hafit style, others of Umm an-Nar, Wadi Suq and Iron Age type, some reused into the Middle Islamic period; Suhaila 1 occupied from the early Islamic era to the mid-20th century; Suhaila 2 and Wadi Jeema larger settlements with agricultural terraces; underground falaj about 560 m long dated to the 1st millennium BCE. Hatta Mountain Reserve record: 2,100 ha in the Hajar Mountains of Dubai, part of the Oman–UAE ophiolite; Ramsar site no. 2368 (9 January 2019); rare mountain freshwater ecosystem; the mountains receive about 30% of the country’s annual rainfall, recharging the aquifer that feeds the Hatta and Al Ghabra dams; 19% of the country’s plant species, 79% of its dragonfly species, 27% of its bird species and 44% of its mammal species. Map distance between the two records: about 5 km.
spec.an: Falaj systems are built, by design, to tap groundwater and lead it to the surface by gravity, and Al Tikriti (2002) argued that the falaj system originated in south-eastern Arabia, with early examples in the Al Ain area. Hydrogeologists commonly compare the chemistry and natural isotopes of water from springs, wells and channels to show whether they draw on one aquifer. No single published case of a falaj and a wetland sharing one source is cited here.
spec.val: Locate the mother well and the line of the Hatta falaj and map the rock and fractures it cuts; sample water from the falaj line, from springs and pools in the reserve and from wells feeding the dams, and compare their chemistry and stable isotopes; map the terraces of Suhaila 2 and Wadi Jeema against springs and the depth of groundwater.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the falaj tapped water held in the gravel of the wadi bed and fed by floods, not groundwater from the fractured ophiolite, so it shares little with the reserve’s springs.
Rival explanation 2: the reserve’s pools and streams are fed mainly by runoff after rain, not by the aquifer, so they and the falaj draw on different water.
Rival explanation 3: the villages and terraces were placed for other reasons, such as safe ground, routes or grazing, and their closeness to water is simply a result of the narrow valleys.
refs: UNESCO World Heritage Centre (2023). Hatta Archaeological Landscape (Emirate of Dubai), Tentative List ref. 6664. https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/6664
Ramsar Sites Information Service. Hatta Mountain Reserve (site no. 2368). https://rsis.ramsar.org/ris/2368
Dubai Municipality. About Dubai Protected Areas. https://www.dm.gov.ae/dubai-protected-areas/about-dubai-protected-areas/
Al Tikriti, W.Y. (2002). The south-east Arabian origin of the falaj system. Proceedings of the Seminar for Arabian Studies 32: 117–138.
spec.se: In the mountains of Hatta, a falaj more than 2,000 years old and a wetland full of dragonflies lie about 5 km apart. Do they drink from the same water stored in the rock? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: في جبال حتا يقع فلج يزيد عمره على 2,000 عام وأرض رطبة تعجّ باليعاسيب، يفصل بينهما نحو 5 كيلومترات. فهل يشربان من الماء نفسه المخزون في الصخر؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from two Hatta records side by side. The archaeological record dates a 560 m underground falaj to the 1st millennium BCE. The reserve record, about 5 km away, says these mountains catch about 30% of the country’s annual rainfall and recharge an aquifer, and that the reserve holds 79% of the country’s dragonfly species. The old channel and the living wetland both need the same thing: water from the rock.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من سجلين متجاورين في حتا. يؤرّخ السجل الأثري فلجًا جوفيًا طوله 560 مترًا بالألفية الأولى قبل الميلاد. ويذكر سجل المحمية، على بعد نحو 5 كيلومترات، أن هذه الجبال تتلقّى نحو 30% من الأمطار السنوية في الدولة وتغذّي خزانًا جوفيًا، وأن المحمية تضم 79% من أنواع اليعاسيب في الدولة. فالقناة القديمة والأرض الرطبة الحية تحتاجان إلى الشيء نفسه: ماء من الصخر.

tag.en: An ancient channel and a dragonfly wetland may share one hidden source
tag.ar: قد تتقاسم قناة قديمة وأرض رطبة لليعاسيب نبعًا خفيًّا واحدًا

en: In the Hatta mountains, people dug an underground channel, a falaj, about 560 m long, in the 1st millennium BCE. Around it lie terraced fields, old villages and more than 70 tombs, in a landscape used from the Early Bronze Age to the recent past.

About 5 km away is the Hatta Mountain Reserve. These mountains catch about 30% of all the rain that falls on the country each year. The water sinks into the rock, and 79% of the country’s kinds of dragonfly live in the reserve.
ar: في جبال حتا حفر الناس قناة جوفية، أي فلجًا، طولها نحو 560 مترًا في الألفية الأولى قبل الميلاد. وحولها مدرجات زراعية وقرى قديمة وأكثر من 70 قبرًا، في مشهد استُخدم منذ العصر البرونزي المبكر حتى الماضي القريب.
وعلى بعد نحو 5 كيلومترات تقع محمية جبال حتا. تتلقّى هذه الجبال نحو 30% من كل الأمطار التي تهطل على الدولة كل عام، فيتسرّب الماء إلى الصخر، وتعيش في المحمية 79% من أنواع اليعاسيب في الدولة.

h2.en: Seen before: the aflaj of south-eastern Arabia
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: أفلاج جنوب شرق الجزيرة العربية

en: A falaj is a clever invention. Its builders dug down until they found water in the ground, then led it along a gently sloping tunnel until it flowed out by itself onto the fields. Researchers have argued that this way of watering fields began in south-eastern Arabia, with early examples near Al Ain.

To learn where the water of a spring or a well comes from, hydrogeologists compare its chemistry and the tiny natural differences in its atoms. Water from the same underground store carries the same fingerprint.
ar: الفلج اختراع ذكي؛ إذ يحفر بناته حتى يبلغوا الماء في جوف الأرض، ثم يقودونه في نفق قليل الانحدار حتى يخرج من تلقاء نفسه إلى الحقول. وقد رأى باحثون أن هذا الأسلوب في الري نشأ في جنوب شرق الجزيرة العربية، وأن له أمثلة مبكرة قرب العين.
ولمعرفة مصدر مياه الينابيع والآبار يقارن علماء المياه الجوفية تركيبها الكيميائي والفروق الطبيعية الدقيقة في ذرّاتها؛ فالماء الآتي من مخزون جوفي واحد يحمل البصمة نفسها.

en: On this map, an ancient channel and a living wetland lie about 5 km apart in mountains made of old ocean crust. If both drink from the same water stored in its cracks, their water will share one fingerprint, and the falaj will follow a crack in the rock.
But perhaps the falaj only caught flood water in the gravel of the wadi. Then the two waters will look different, and the idea falls.
ar: على هذه الخريطة تقع قناة قديمة وأرض رطبة حية على بعد نحو 5 كيلومترات إحداهما من الأخرى، في جبال من قشرة محيطية قديمة. فإن كانتا تشربان من الماء نفسه المخزون في شقوقها، فستحمل مياههما بصمة واحدة، وسيتبع الفلج شقًّا في الصخر.
لكن ربما لم يجمع الفلج إلا مياه السيول من حصى الوادي. وعندها ستبدو المياه مختلفة، وتسقط الفكرة.

spec.te: Was Wasit Once Part of Sharjah’s Sheltered Water?
spec.ta: هل كانت واسط يومًا جزءًا من مياه الشارقة المحمية؟
spec.desc: A connection between three records on this map. Wasit Nature Reserve, an inland lake and wetland complex of Sharjah and a Ramsar site, was once a tidal lagoon, which its record says makes it useful for understanding how the coastline has changed. The old port of Sharjah lies in a protected sea inlet, Al Khor, at a place where the geographer Al Idrisi referred to a port in the 11th century. Up the coast, the Umm Al Quwain spit record dates the life of a lagoon on this same shore: sea level about 2 m higher than today around 5,500 BP, the lagoon at its largest around 3,500 BP, and a ridge that nearly closed it by about 1,500 BP. The idea: Wasit and the Sharjah inlet are two pieces of one mid-Holocene lagoon, cut apart as the sea fell and sand ridges grew, so that the sheltered water that made Sharjah a port is the last open part of a lagoon whose inland end became Wasit.
spec.sig: If true, the reserve would hold the buried story of how Sharjah’s harbour was formed, and its sediments would show when the sheltered water that made the port possible began to shrink.
spec.ev: Wasit Nature Reserve record: 86 ha inland lake and wetland complex; Ramsar site no. 2386 (9 May 2019); once a tidal lagoon, useful for understanding how the coastline has changed; mudflats, lakes, dunes, reed beds and thickets with at least 144 bird species; protected area since 2007. Sharjah: the Gate to Trucial States record: UNESCO Tentative List 2014; the port lies in a protected sea inlet (Al Khor); Al Idrisi referred to a port here in the 11th century; the most important port of the lower Arabian Gulf into the first half of the 19th century. Umm Al Quwain spit record: sea level about 2 m higher around 5,500 BP and about 1.5 m higher around 4,500 BP; lagoon at its maximum around 3,500 BP; southern ridge breached around 2,600 BP; a ridge nearly closed the lagoon by about 1,500 BP (Forti et al. 2024). Map distances: Wasit to the old port of Sharjah about 8 km; Wasit to the Umm Al Quwain spit about 22 km.
spec.an: Evans and colleagues (1969) showed on the coast of Abu Dhabi that, over the last few thousand years, the shoreline built out seaward and old lagoons and tidal flats were left behind inland as salt flats. Forti and colleagues (2024) traced how the Umm Al Quwain lagoon grew, was breached and was nearly closed by sand ridges as the sea fell from its mid-Holocene high.
spec.val: Drill a line of cores across Wasit and along the low ground between it and the Sharjah inlet; look for lagoon muds and marine shells and date them by radiocarbon; map buried channels with ground-penetrating radar; compare the ages with the Umm Al Quwain sequence.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: Wasit was a separate lagoon with its own opening to the sea and was never joined to the Sharjah inlet.
Rival explanation 2: Wasit stayed tidal until much more recent times and was cut off by modern building rather than by the natural fall of the sea.
Rival explanation 3: the Sharjah inlet is a younger feature, opened by a later breach of the coastal ridge, so it is not the remnant of an older, larger lagoon.

UNESCO World Heritage Centre. Sharjah: the Gate to Trucial States (Tentative List ref. 5941). https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5941

Forti, L., Degli Esposti, M., Cremaschi, M., Borgi, F., Azzoni, R.S. & Zerboni, A. (2024). Geomorphological evolution of the Umm al-Quwain (UAE) coastal-lagoon system: Natural processes and recent human impact. Catena 247, 108517. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.catena.2024.108517
Evans, G. et al. (1969). Stratigraphy and geologic history of the sabkha, Abu Dhabi. Sedimentology 12.
spec.se: Wasit, now an inland wetland of Sharjah, was once a tidal lagoon. Was it the inner end of the same sheltered water that made Sharjah a port? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: كانت واسط، وهي اليوم أرض رطبة داخلية في الشارقة، بحيرة مدّ وجزر في الماضي. فهل كانت الطرف الداخلي للمياه المحمية نفسها التي جعلت من الشارقة ميناءً؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

en: Wasit Nature Reserve is an inland wetland of lakes, mudflats and reeds, where at least 144 kinds of birds have been seen. Its record holds a surprise: it was once a tidal lagoon, where the sea came and went with the tide.
About 8 km away, the old port of Sharjah lies in a protected sea inlet. Already in the 11th century, the geographer Al Idrisi wrote of a port here.
ar: محمية واسط أرض رطبة داخلية من البحيرات والسهول الطينية والقصب، رُصد فيها ما لا يقل عن 144 نوعًا من الطيور. وفي سجلها مفاجأة: كانت يومًا بحيرة مدّ وجزر، يأتيها البحر ويرحل عنها مع المدّ والجزر.

h2.en: Seen before: the coasts of Abu Dhabi and Umm Al Quwain
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: ساحلا أبوظبي وأم القيوين

en: On the coast of Abu Dhabi, Evans and colleagues showed in 1969 how, over the last few thousand years, the shore built out into the sea and left old lagoons and tidal flats stranded inland as salt flats.

At Umm Al Quwain, Forti and colleagues dated the whole life of a lagoon: the sea stood about 2 m higher around 5,500 years ago, the lagoon was largest around 3,500 years ago, and a sand ridge had nearly closed it by about 1,500 years ago.
ar: على ساحل أبوظبي بيّن إيفانز وزملاؤه عام 1969 كيف امتد الشاطئ نحو البحر خلال الآلاف القليلة الأخيرة من السنين، تاركًا بحيرات ساحلية ومسطحات مدّية قديمة معزولة في الداخل، فصارت سبخات.
وفي أم القيوين أرّخ فورتي وزملاؤه حياة بحيرة ساحلية كاملة: كان البحر أعلى بنحو مترين قبل نحو 5,500 عام، وبلغت البحيرة أقصى اتساعها قبل نحو 3,500 عام، ثم كاد حاجز رملي يغلقها قبل نحو 1,500 عام.

en: On this map, an inland wetland that was once a lagoon lies about 8 km from a sheltered harbour. If they are two pieces of one lagoon, cores will find the same old lagoon mud running between them, and the inland end will have been cut off first.
But perhaps Wasit was always a lagoon of its own. Then a barrier will lie between them, and the idea falls.
ar: على هذه الخريطة تقع أرض رطبة داخلية كانت يومًا بحيرة ساحلية على بعد نحو 8 كيلومترات من ميناء محمي. فإن كانتا قطعتين من بحيرة واحدة، فستجد العينات الطين البحيري القديم نفسه ممتدًا بينهما، وسيكون الطرف الداخلي قد انقطع أولًا.
لكن ربما كانت واسط بحيرة مستقلة منذ البداية. وعندها سيظهر حاجز بينهما، وتسقط الفكرة.

spec.n: The Creek’s Gift to the Flamingos
spec.te: Did Dredging the Creek Feed Ras Al Khor?
spec.ta: هل غذّى تجريف الخور محمية رأس الخور؟
spec.desc: A connection between two records on this map in the heart of Dubai. Khor Dubai is a natural seawater inlet of the Arabian Gulf about 14 km long and 100 to 500 m wide, dredged in 1961 to admit vessels drawing 2.1 m. At its inner end lies Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary, 620 ha of mangrove, lagoon, intertidal mud and sand flats and saline flats, where more than 20,000 waterbirds of 67 species winter, including more than 3,000 greater flamingos. The idea: deepening the creek changed the way the tide moves along it, so that since 1961 more fine mud has been carried to its quiet inner end and settled there, and part of the mudflats that feed the sanctuary’s birds is a by-product of the city’s harbour works.
spec.sig: If true, the richness of the sanctuary would be partly an unplanned result of engineering, and future work on the creek could add to, or take away, the mud that its birds depend on.
spec.ev: Khor Dubai record: natural seawater inlet about 14 km long and 100–500 m wide, dividing Bur Dubai and Deira and ending at Ras Al Khor; Dubai first recorded in 1587; dredged in 1961 to admit vessels drawing 2.1 m; UNESCO Tentative List 2012 for its first 4.5 km. Ras Al Khor record: 620 ha sanctuary of mangrove, lagoon, intertidal mud and sand flats and saline flats at the end of the 14 km creek; Ramsar site since 29 August 2007; more than 20,000 waterbirds of 67 species in winter, including more than 3,000 greater flamingos; more than 1% of the regional population of broad-billed sandpipers; over 450 animal and 47 plant species. Umm Al Quwain spit record (for comparison): grey mangrove cover has expanded since 1984 as dredging improved tidal flushing. Map distance between the creek record and the sanctuary record: about 8 km.
spec.an: The Umm Al Quwain spit record on this same map already notes that grey mangrove cover there has expanded since 1984 as dredging improved tidal flushing (Forti et al. 2024). More widely, coastal scientists have described estuaries where deepening a channel for ships changed the tides and the amount of mud carried inland. Recent mud layers are commonly dated with the radioactive elements lead-210 and caesium-137. No single published case is cited here for a creek and a bird sanctuary.
spec.val: Take sediment cores in the mudflats of Ras Al Khor and date their recent layers with lead-210 and caesium-137; compare how fast mud built up before and after 1961; study old aerial photographs and maps of the end of the creek; and model the tides in the creek before and after dredging.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the mudflats are much older and grew at a steady rate, and the dredging made no measurable difference.
Rival explanation 2: the extra mud comes mainly from land reclamation and building works around the end of the creek, not from changes in the tide.
Rival explanation 3: deepening the creek flushed its inner end more strongly and removed mud, and the birds gather there for other reasons, such as the protection of the sanctuary.

spec.se: Dubai Creek was dredged in 1961, and at its quiet inner end more than 3,000 flamingos now feed on the mud. Did the harbour works help build that mud? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: جُرف خور دبي عام 1961، وعند طرفه الداخلي الهادئ تتغذّى اليوم أكثر من 3,000 من طيور الفلامنغو على الطين. فهل أسهمت أعمال الميناء في بناء هذا الطين؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from the two ends of one creek. The Khor Dubai record says the creek was dredged in 1961. The Ras Al Khor record, at its inner end about 8 km away, describes intertidal mudflats that feed more than 20,000 wintering waterbirds. And the Umm Al Quwain spit record shows that dredging has already changed another lagoon on this coast.

tag.en: Deepening Dubai Creek may have helped to build a wetland
tag.ar: ربما أسهم تعميق خور دبي في بناء أرض رطبة

en: Dubai Creek is a natural arm of the Arabian Gulf, about 14 km long, with Bur Dubai on one side and Deira on the other. In 1961 it was dredged, made deeper so that boats needing 2.1 m of water could come in.
At its quiet inner end lies Ras Al Khor, 620 hectares of mangrove, lagoon and soft mud. Each winter more than 20,000 waterbirds feed there, among them more than 3,000 pink flamingos.
ar: خور دبي ذراع طبيعية من الخليج العربي طولها نحو 14 كيلومترًا، تقع بر دبي على إحدى ضفتيها وديرة على الأخرى. وفي عام 1961 جُرف الخور وعُمّق لتدخله سفن يبلغ غاطسها 2.1 متر.
وعند طرفه الداخلي الهادئ تقع محمية رأس الخور: 620 هكتارًا من القرم والبحيرات والطين اللين. وفي كل شتاء تتغذّى هناك أكثر من 20,000 من الطيور المائية، بينها أكثر من 3,000 من طيور الفلامنغو الوردية.

h2.en: Seen before: a lagoon changed by dredging
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: بحيرة غيّرها التجريف

en: Up the coast at Umm Al Quwain, scientists found that grey mangroves have spread since 1984, because dredging let the tide flow in and out more freely.

In other parts of the world too, deepening a channel for ships has changed the tides and the amount of mud they carry. Scientists can date recent mud layers by the tiny traces of radioactive elements trapped inside them.
ar: إلى الشمال على الساحل، في أم القيوين، وجد العلماء أن أشجار القرم الرمادية انتشرت منذ عام 1984، لأن التجريف سمح للمدّ والجزر بالدخول والخروج بحرية أكبر.
وفي أماكن أخرى من العالم أيضًا، غيّر تعميق القنوات للسفن حركةَ المدّ والجزر ومقدارَ الطين الذي تحمله. ويستطيع العلماء تأريخ طبقات الطين الحديثة بآثار دقيقة من عناصر مشعة محبوسة فيها.

en: On this map, a dredged creek leads straight to a wetland full of birds. If deepening the creek sent more mud to its quiet end, cores from Ras Al Khor will show mud piling up faster after 1961 than before.
But perhaps the mud built up the same way for centuries, or came from building works. The mud layers will tell.
ar: على هذه الخريطة يقود خور مجروف مباشرة إلى أرض رطبة تعجّ بالطيور. فإن كان تعميق الخور قد أرسل مزيدًا من الطين إلى طرفه الهادئ، فستُظهر العينات من رأس الخور أن الطين تراكم بعد عام 1961 أسرع مما كان قبله.
لكن ربما تراكم الطين بالطريقة نفسها قرونًا، أو جاء من أعمال البناء. وطبقات الطين هي التي ستحكم.
